articles.summaryTr: ABD borsalarında teknoloji hisseleri öncülüğünde yaşanan sert satış dalgası kripto para piyasasını da vurdu. Bitcoin gün içinde 76 bin doların altını görürken, küresel kripto para piyasasının toplam değeri 24 saatte 108 milyar dolardan fazla azaldı.
articles.articleText: Bitcoin 76 bin doların altına geriledi! Kripto piyasasında sert satış dalgası - ABD borsalarında teknoloji hisseleri öncülüğünde yaşanan sert satış dalgası kripto para piyasasını da vurdu. Bitcoin gün içinde 76 bin doların altını görürken, küresel kripto para piyasasının toplam değeri 24 saatte 108 milyar dolardan fazla azaldı. CoinMarketCap verilerine göre, küresel kripto para piyasasının toplam değeri son 24 saatte yüzde 4,22 düşerek 2,56 trilyon dolara geriledi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Piyasanın en büyük kripto para birimi Bitcoin, son 24 saatte yüzde 4,6 değer kaybederken haftalık kaybı da yüzde 5'i aştı. Gün içinde 76 bin doların altına gerileyen Bitcoin, TSİ 23.00 itibarıyla 76 bin 241 dolardan işlem gördü. Altcoin piyasasında da satış baskısı etkili oldu. Ethereum'un fiyatı son 24 saatte yüzde 6,1 düşerek 2 bin 258 dolara indi. Wall Street'teki satış dalgası kriptoyu da vurdu Kripto para piyasasındaki düşüşte ABD borsalarında yaşanan sert satışlar etkili oldu. Ara seçimlerin ardından özellikle teknoloji hisselerinde yoğunlaşan satış baskısı, riskli varlıklara yönelik iştahı zayıflattı. Demokratların ara seçimlerde elde ettiği zafer sonrasında Kongre'de oluşan yeni siyasi dengeler, yapay zeka ve veri merkezi sektörlerine yönelik denetimlerin sıkılaşabileceği endişelerini artırdı. Bu gelişme, teknoloji şirketlerinin hisselerinde satışları derinleştirdi. Gün içinde Dow Jones endeksi 1000 puanın üzerinde değer kaybederek yüzde 3'e yakın geriledi. S&P 500 yüzde 3'ün, Nasdaq ise yüzde 4'ün üzerinde düşüş kaydetti. Kripto düzenlemelerinde belirsizlik artıyor Demokratların Kongre'de çoğunluğu ele geçirmesinin dijital varlık sektörüne yönelik düzenlemelerin geleceği konusunda da belirsizlik yarattığı değerlendiriliyor. Sektörün yakından takip ettiği ve dijital varlıklara yönelik kapsamlı bir düzenleyici çerçeve oluşturmayı amaçlayan CLARITY Act'in Kongre'den geçmesine ilişkin beklentiler de zayıfladı. Düzenlemenin yasalaşmasına yönelik sürecin yıl sonuna kadar ilerleme kaydetmesinin düşük ihtimal olarak görülmesi, kripto piyasasındaki belirsizliği artıran unsurlar arasında yer alıyor.

articles.title: California governor commutes death sentences for all 548 people on death row
articles.summary: California has historically had the largest population of death row inmates in the US.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: California governor commutes death sentences for all 548 people on death row
articles.summaryTr: California has historically had the largest population of death row inmates in the US.
articles.articleText: California governor commutes death sentences for all 548 people on death row - Published California Governor Gavin Newsom has commuted the death sentences of all 548 people on death row in the state, changing them instead with life in prison. "We can now let these offenders die in obscurity while we forever remember and honour the victims," he said in a letter. The decision to spare death row inmates is largely symbolic in a state that has not executed a prisoner since 2006, though experts say it could save millions of dollars in court costs each year. Only 13 inmates have been executed since voters reinstated the death penalty in 1978. The decision comes as Newsom, the Democratic leader of the most populous US state, has been discussed as a possible 2028 contender for president. Newsom, who is term limited, is winding down his final months in office. Fellow Democrat Xavier Becerra is projected to take over after the midterm elections on Tuesday. Newsom explained in his letter that he is exercising his constitutional clemency authority to commute the sentences to life without the possibility of parole. "After nearly 30 years in public office, I have come to understand the limits of what government can justly accomplish," Newsom said. "I take this action because I firmly believe that state-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California's values, undermines the foundations of our legal system and diminishes each of us". California has historically had the largest population of death row inmates. Newsom had previously ordered a halt to the death penalty in the state in 2019. Newsom, describing his decision as a difficult but "righteous action", said that although many Californians feel that those who commit brutal crimes deserve to die, he has concluded that "the state cannot morally kill them". He said that by every measure, California's system for administering the death penalty "is a failure", and that it has not and cannot be fairly applied, resulting in the conviction of innocent people. Life without the possibility of parole is the most severe punishment he can lawfully impose and that the state can ethically enforce, he said. He acknowledged that his clemency action will anger and hurt some Californians and said that it will "always weigh heavily on me". "As Governor, I alone bear responsibility for this decision and its impact, just as I alone would bear responsibility for each execution," he wrote. "For this reason I am compelled to follow my conscience and, as authorised by our Constitution, take this action for the welfare of the State of California." Because individual states have the power to prosecute crimes and order executions, much of the power lies with state governors. The decision comes after the high-profile botched execution of a woman in Tennessee in late September and while executions have been on the rise in the US. On the federal level, President Donald Trump, a long-time supporter of the death penalty, has described capital punishment as "an essential tool for deterring and punishing those who would commit the most heinous crimes and acts of lethal violence against American citizens". In 2020, during his first term, he ended a nearly two-decade moratorium on the federal death penalty, by ordering 13 executions over a six-month period. While the moratorium returned under President Biden, on the first day of Trump's second term in 2025, he signed an executive order that re-instated the death penalty. No federal executions have been carried out since he signed it, however. In the US, both the federal government and local states authorities can order executions. articles.title: Who could be behind hoax bomb threats to European air travel?
articles.summary: There is no hard evidence so far linking airline bomb threats to Russia, Iran or any proxy groups.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Who could be behind hoax bomb threats to European air travel?
articles.summaryTr: There is no hard evidence so far linking airline bomb threats to Russia, Iran or any proxy groups.
articles.articleText: Who could be behind hoax bomb threats to European air travel? - Published The warnings came in thick and fast, targeting one airline or airport after another. In nearly all cases - London's Heathrow airport being a notable exception - they were taken to be credible enough to divert the aircraft in question, or even in Italy's case, to scramble fighter jets to escort it. They all turned out to be false, which does not, of course, mean that the next ones will not be real. It is hardly surprising that the simultaneous, co-ordinated nature of these airline hoaxes, coupled with other malicious actions across Europe, are causing some people to point the finger of suspicion at Russia. Following a series of cyber-attacks and mysterious drone sightings over sensitive sites earlier this year, in the past few days we have seen the remote hacking of supermarket freezers, as well as a blood bank, a suspicious incident on Poland's border with Russia, and in August a drone attack Germany's Leipzig Halle airport which its interior minister publicly blamed on Moscow. So is Russia behind this? There are many who argue, based purely on circumstantial evidence, that this must surely be yet another example of "hybrid", "grey zone" or "sub-threshold" warfare - actions that damage a nation's infrastructure or society but which tend to be anonymous, deniable and which fall short of triggering Nato's Article 5 and thereby mobilising a response by the West. Moscow is certainly furious with Nato for supporting Ukraine and, in doing so, frustrating the Kremlin's plans to swallow up that country and effectively terminate its independence. Russian bloggers have also suggested that, if Ukraine's drones are currently making Russia's airports unsafe, and Western sanctions are blocking Russian airlines from European airspace, then why shouldn't Western nations feel the same pain? But as of Thursday evening no hard evidence had emerged linking the airline hoaxes to Russia, Iran or any proxy groups controlled by them. There is the email threat sent on Thursday morning to airport authorities in Rome, purporting to be from "Fighters of the Male State". That name likely refers to the Russian group Muzhskoi Legion or "Male Legion", an ultra-right group with such extreme views it was banned by a Moscow court in 2021. Yet, it retained tens of thousands of online followers on Telegram as it cheered on the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine in the following year. But the email sent to Rome, even if genuine - and who is to say it is not another group hiding behind that name? - is unlikely to provide the leads that police and airport authorities need to pin down who is generating these hoaxes and why. For national police forces, airport authorities and transport ministries trying to work out who is behind these hoaxes and how best to mitigate their effect when they happen again, the task is not to go with who they think might be the most likely culprits but instead to follow the cold, hard leads - if they can find them.

articles.title: Fon soruşturması kapsamında sıcak gelişme: Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya hakkında tutuklama talebi
articles.summary: İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı'nın yürüttüğü fon soruşturmasında Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya, tutuklama talebiyle mahkemeye sevk edildi. Kaya hakkındaki nihai kararı mahkeme verecek.

articles.titleTr: Fon soruşturması kapsamında sıcak gelişme: Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya hakkında tutuklama talebi
articles.summaryTr: İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı'nın yürüttüğü fon soruşturmasında Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya, tutuklama talebiyle mahkemeye sevk edildi. Kaya hakkındaki nihai kararı mahkeme verecek.
articles.articleText: Fon soruşturması kapsamında sıcak gelişme: Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya hakkında tutuklama talebi YAYIN TARİHİ, 05 Kasım 2026 22:46 GÜNCELLEME, 05 Kasım 2026 23:13 PAYLAŞ - İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı'nın yürüttüğü fon soruşturmasında Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya, tutuklama talebiyle mahkemeye sevk edildi. Kaya hakkındaki nihai kararı mahkeme verecek. İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı tarafından yürütülen fon soruşturması kapsamında Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya, tutuklama talebiyle mahkemeye sevk edildi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Soruşturma kapsamında savcılıktaki işlemleri tamamlanan Kaya hakkında tutuklama talebinde bulunuldu. Mahkemenin, tutuklama talebine ilişkin karar vermesi bekleniyor. Fon soruşturması kapsamında "şüpheli" sıfatıyla ifadesi alınan İlyas Kaya ile eski SPK Başkanı İbrahim Ömer Gönül, haklarında adli kontrol uygulanması talebiyle hakimliğe sevk edildi.

articles.summaryTr: 2027 yılı bütçe görüşmelerinde Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığı bütçesine 33 milyar TL ilave ödenek ayrılmasını öngören önerge gündeme geldi. Kaynak, Halkbank aracılığıyla esnaf ve sanatkârlara kullandırılan faiz destekli krediler için kullanılacak.
articles.articleText: Bütçeye ek ödenek geliyor: Esnafa 33 milyar TL’lik kredi desteği! - 2027 yılı bütçe görüşmelerinde Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığı bütçesine 33 milyar TL ilave ödenek ayrılmasını öngören önerge gündeme geldi. Kaynak, Halkbank aracılığıyla esnaf ve sanatkârlara kullandırılan faiz destekli krediler için kullanılacak. TBMM’de 2027 yılı bütçe görüşmeleri sırasında esnaf ve sanatkârları yakından ilgilendiren önemli bir önerge sunuldu. Önergeyle, Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığı bütçesine 33 milyar TL tutarında ilave ödenek eklenmesi teklif edildi. 33 milyar TL Halkbank kredileri için ayrılacak CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Önergenin gerekçesinde, 5570 sayılı Kamu Sermayeli Bankalar Tarafından Yürütülen Faiz Destekli Kredi ve Kâr Payı Destekli Fon Kullandırılmasına Dair Kanun'a atıfta bulunuldu. Buna göre 33 milyar TL'lik ödenek, Türkiye Halk Bankası A.Ş. tarafından esnaf ve sanatkârların finansman ihtiyaçlarının uygun koşullarda karşılanabilmesi amacıyla kullandırılan destekli krediler için Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığı bütçesine eklenecek. 2027 bütçesine 33 milyar TL ilave ödenek Önergeye ilişkin cetvelde bütçe bilgileri şöyle sıralandı: - Kurum: Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığı - Yıl: 2027 - Program: 17 - Kurumsal kod: 12.40 - Finansman kodu: 01 - Ekonomik kod: 05.01 - Eklenen tutar: 33 milyar TL Önergenin gerekçesinde, ilave ödeneğin esnaf ve sanatkârların finansman ihtiyaçlarının uygun koşullarda karşılanmasını teminen ayrıldığı belirtildi.

Buna göre 33 milyar TL'lik ödenek, Türkiye Halk Bankası A.Ş. tarafından esnaf ve sanatkârların finansman ihtiyaçlarının uygun koşullarda karşılanabilmesi amacıyla kullandırılan destekli krediler için Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığı bütçesine eklenecek. 2027 bütçesine 33 milyar TL ilave ödenek Önergeye ilişkin cetvelde bütçe bilgileri şöyle sıralandı: - Kurum: Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığı - Yıl: 2027 - Program: 17 - Kurumsal kod: 12.40 - Finansman kodu: 01 - Ekonomik kod: 05.01 - Eklenen tutar: 33 milyar TL Önergenin gerekçesinde, ilave ödeneğin esnaf ve sanatkârların finansman ihtiyaçlarının uygun koşullarda karşılanmasını teminen ayrıldığı belirtildi.

articles.articleText: Eight killed in series of shootings in western Turkey - Published Eight people have been killed and one seriously injured in a series of shootings in western Turkey. The attacks took place in the Afyonkarahisar province on Thursday, with victims found in several locations in three separate vehicles, according to local reports. The suspect fled, triggering a manhunt, and authorities later said he had been arrested in Eskişehir province. CCTV footage published in Turkish media showed a man in a black jacket, white trousers and glasses clutching a long weapon as he stood by a red minivan. Turkey's state-run Anadolu Agency reported that three people were killed near Ayazini village and three others near Kiyir village. In Yukaritandir, two women were found injured and later died in hospital. Two teachers were reportedly among the dead. Local media said roads leading to the affected villages were closed by police, while officers launched a large-scale operation to find the suspect. The newspaper Milliyet reported that a vehicle allegedly taken by the attacker had been later found stuck in mud - the suspect having abandoned it before fleeing on foot. In a statement posted on social media, the Afyonkarahisar Governorate said "all relevant institutions of our state have been working in coordination since the very first moment and are meticulously carrying out the necessary work".

articles.summary: The US first lady was credited by all for playing a key though unspecified role in the ceasefire.

articles.titleTr: Melania Trump calls for lasting Ukraine truce as she hosts Russian and Ukrainian officials
articles.summaryTr: The US first lady was credited by all for playing a key though unspecified role in the ceasefire.
articles.articleText: Melania Trump calls for lasting Ukraine truce as she hosts Russian and Ukrainian officials - Published US First Lady Melania Trump called for a "more enduring" ceasefire in Ukraine as she welcomed Russian and Ukrainian delegations at the White House following last week's truce in the southern region of Kherson. Hundreds of residents of the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky facing starvation and constant bombardment were able to evacuate during a six-day ceasefire, which both Moscow and Kyiv credited Trump with brokering. "The lives of innocent people must transcend the division of war. I hope Oleshky inspires greater peace," she said. The unusual White House event saw senior Ukrainian and Russian officials meet away from the setting of official US-brokered peace talks they have been holding without success since last year. The delegations were made up of Ukraine's human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets and his Russian counterpart Yana Lantratova, as well as Ukrainian MP Davyd Arakhamia and Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev. Melania Trump was credited by all for playing a key though unspecified role in the ceasefire, and all parties conveyed to her the gratitude of the Russian and Ukrainian presidents. The US first lady said she had "reviewed demining plans, aerial images, assessed roadways, and discussed evacuation routes, hospital access, vehicles, and medical resources" during the truce. "Last week in Oleshky and neighbouring areas of Kherson, people experienced the simple joys of life for the first time since 2022," Trump said. "They walked down familiar streets without fear of explosions." She thanked both Volodymyr Zelensky and Vladimir Putin, making no reference to the origins of the war, which began when the Russian president launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, and which has caused thousands of civilian casualties and the displacement of millions. Dmitriev, a businessman and Kremlin special envoy who has previously represented Moscow during peace talks with Ukraine, thanked Trump for "saving and touching so many lives". "Let us continue making a humanitarian contribution together; this is within our power," Dmitriev said, before gifting Melania Trump a framed drawing by an 11-year-old Oleshky evacuee. He also praised Trump for her work on reuniting children separated from their families by the war. These include children allegedly abducted by Russia. Arakhamia, a Ukrainian MP who heads Zelensky's party in parliament who has also been part of the Ukrainian negotiating team, said the Oleshky ceasefire had constituted the "biggest de-escalation since 2022". "We are creating a momentum where both sides are learning the… mechanics of how to actually keep the peace when the peace comes," he added. He acknowledged that the "political track" of negotiations to end the conflict was "complex" but said Ukrainians were asking Melania Trump "to keep going and find new missions and de-escalate more." At the end of the event, Trump handed Dmitriev and Arakhamia two letters to be hand-delivered to their respective presidents. The White House later said Melania Trump had invited her guests to view two historic artifacts which she had "personally selected as powerful symbols of peace". One was an 18th Century medicine chest which was removed from the White House when the British set it on fire in 1812. "Once adversaries, the United States and Great Britain ultimately established a strong alliance," the White House said. The second artifact was a cup gifted in 1899 to the French ambassador in recognition of his efforts to bring the Spanish-American war to an end. Melania Trump has generally remained discreet on foreign policy matters, and neither Moscow nor Kyiv have elaborated on the nature or extent of her involvement in coordinating the delicate ceasefire - the most enduring and widespread of the war so far. A source who works in the local government of the Kherson region told the BBC that work on the Oleshky evacuation had been ongoing for almost a year. However, the source said, "at a certain point other individuals became involved, seemingly after most of the groundwork had already been laid and subsequently began taking credit for the progress that had been made." It was difficult to determine exactly who had played what role and at which stage of the process, the source acknowledged, adding that "those who had been directly involved in the negotiations for nearly a year were eventually prohibited from communicating publicly about the matter." Speaking after the meeting in the White House had taken place, President Zelensky said the success of the Oleshky ceasefire "had proved a very simple thing: when Putin wants the fighting to stop, it stops." "The same applies to our people who are held in Russian captivity. When Putin wants, they go home." A source close to American officials shared a similar assessment, implying to the BBC that despite the outward praise, "the person who made [the ceasefire] possible, whether we like it or not, is essentially Putin." "And this was done in order to pass the ball to [Donald] Trump... so that it would have some positive effect for his midterm elections." There has been no change whatsoever in Russia's position, Ukrainian political analyst Dmytro Levus told the BBC. Moscow "agreed to it because there was pressure from the American side... In doing so, the Russians confirmed Zelenskyy's words that, when necessary, it turns out Russia can quickly stop firing and even maintain that ceasefire." As the frontline region of Kherson experienced its first six days of peace in several years, the rest of Ukraine continued to come under Russian attack. This week, several drone and missile attacks killed and injured civilians across the country. On Monday alone, more than 40 people were killed in a single Russian strike on an aid distribution centre in the region of Zaporizhzhia. More are thought to still be buried under the rubble. Additional reporting by Anastasiia Levchenko in Kyiv

articles.titleTr: Bakan Mehmet Şimşek'ten fon soruşturmasında dikkat çeken çıkış: Listeler açıklansın
articles.summaryTr: Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı Mehmet Şimşek, fon soruşturmasında listelerin açıklanmasını şahsen istediğini belirtti. Şimşek, bilgiye dayalı çıkışların tespit edilmesi halinde suç duyurusunda bulunulduğunu ve soruşturmada kimseye taviz verilmeyeceğini söyledi.
articles.articleText: Bakan Mehmet Şimşek'ten fon soruşturmasında dikkat çeken çıkış: Listeler açıklansın - Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı Mehmet Şimşek, fon soruşturmasında listelerin açıklanmasını şahsen istediğini belirtti. Şimşek, bilgiye dayalı çıkışların tespit edilmesi halinde suç duyurusunda bulunulduğunu ve soruşturmada kimseye taviz verilmeyeceğini söyledi. Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı Mehmet Şimşek, Türkiye Büyük Millet Meclisi'nde (TBMM) milletvekillerinin sorularını yanıtladı. Şimşek, sermaye piyasalarında yaşanan gelişmeler, fon soruşturması, Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu'nun (SPK) yetkileri ve Mali Suçları Araştırma Kurulu'nun (MASAK) süreçteki rolüne ilişkin açıklamalarda bulundu. "Listelerin açıklanmasını şahsen isterim" CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Fon soruşturması kapsamında gerçekleştirilen çıkışlara ilişkin değerlendirmelerde bulunan Şimşek, çıkışların bilgiye dayandığının belirlenmesi halinde ilgililer hakkında suç duyurusunda bulunduklarını söyledi. Listelerin kamuoyuyla paylaşılmasına ilişkin de konuşan Şimşek, "Listelerin açıklanmasında engel yok, ben şahsen açıklanmasını isterim." ifadelerini kullandı. "Hazine'nin 1 kuruşu tasfiyede kullanılmadı" Fonların tasfiye sürecine ilişkin açıklamalarda bulunan Şimşek, tasfiye işlemlerinde Hazine kaynaklarının kullanılmadığını belirtti. Şimşek, "Hazine'nin 1 kuruşu tasfiyede kullanılmadı." dedi. "İhmali ve suistimali olan varsa hesap verecektir" Fon soruşturmasında ihmali veya suistimali bulunanların hesap vereceğini belirten Şimşek, "Bu süreçte ihmali ve suistimali olan varsa hesap verecektir. Vermeye başladılar." ifadelerini kullandı. Daha önce görev yapan SPK başkanlarıyla ilgili soruşturma başlatıldığını aktaran Şimşek, önceki başkan hakkında soruşturma izni verildiğini söyledi. Şimşek, fon soruşturmasında kim olursa olsun hiçbir şekilde taviz verilmeyeceğini vurguladı. SPK'nın yetkilerine ilişkin açıklama Sermaye piyasalarında inceleme ve yaptırım yetkisinin SPK'ya verildiğini belirten Şimşek, bakanın şahsen bu alanlarda piyasaya doğrudan müdahale etme veya düzenleme yapma yetkisinin bulunmadığını ifade etti. Risklerin gündemlerine gelmesinden itibaren ellerindeki bütün araçları kullandıklarını söyleyen Şimşek, 4 Kasım'da kamuoyunu ve ilgili paydaşları uyardıklarını, ancak uyarmakla yetinmediklerini belirtti. MASAK'ın rolüne ilişkin değerlendirme MASAK'ın süreçteki rolüne ilişkin çok sayıda soru yöneltildiğini belirten Şimşek, Türkiye'de sermaye hareketlerinin serbest olduğunu ve MASAK'ın işlemler gerçekleşmeden müdahale edemeyeceğini söyledi. Fonların temerrüde düşmesi ve tasfiye kararı alınmasının ardından MASAK'ın işlem erteleme sürecini kendisinin paylaştığını belirten Şimşek, şüpheli işlem bildirimi bulunmaması durumunda MASAK'ın devreye girmesinin işin doğasına aykırı olduğunu ifade etti. 401 milyar liralık hareketin dörtte üçü fon içi işlem Fonlardan 401 milyar lira çekilip çekilmediğine ilişkin soruya da yanıt veren Şimşek, söz konusu tutarın dörtte üçünün yatırımcı çıkışı olmadığını, fon içi hareketlerden oluştuğunu belirtti. Fonların kuruluşundan tasfiyesine kadar gerçekleştirilen bütün işlemlerin incelendiğini söyleyen Şimşek, kapalı oldukları dönemler dahil tüm işlemlerin kayıt altında bulunduğunu ifade etti. Sorumluların mal varlıklarına tedbir uygulanıyor Savcılık ve ilgili kurumların araştırma ve incelemelerini sürdürdüğünü belirten Şimşek, sorumluların mal varlıklarına tedbir konulduğunu ve bunların Tasarruf Mevduatı Sigorta Fonu'nun (TMSF) geri kazanım hesabına devredildiğini söyledi. "Ara ödemelerden stopaj kesintisi yapılmadı" Fonların tasfiye sürecinde yapılan ödemelerden stopaj kesildiği yönündeki iddialara da yanıt veren Şimşek, böyle bir durumun söz konusu olmadığını belirtti. Ara ödemelerden tevkifat yapılmadığını ifade eden Şimşek, normal tasfiye sürecinde para piyasası fonlarında nemalar dahil tüm ödemelerin gerçekleştirildiğini söyledi. articles.title: Fed, OCC check US banks after Binance hack as experts flag security risks
articles.summary: US regulators reportedly contacted banks following last week’s $6.3 billion Binance security hack, while experts raised concerns about transaction security and crypto risks.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Fed, OCC check US banks after Binance hack as experts flag security risks
articles.summaryTr: US regulators reportedly contacted banks following last week’s $6.3 billion Binance security hack, while experts raised concerns about transaction security and crypto risks.
articles.articleText: Fed, OCC check US banks after Binance hack as experts flag security risks US regulators reportedly contacted banks following last week’s $6.3 billion Binance security hack, while experts raised concerns about transaction security and crypto risks. US regulators reportedly contacted banks following last week’s $6.3 billion Binance hack, as cybersecurity experts raised concerns about how financial institutions handle crypto-related security risks. Officials from the Federal Reserve and Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) began contacting banks on Monday to ask about “unusual activity” or service disruptions, Reuters reported Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter. The reported inquiries could be followed by closer attention to how banks manage crypto-related risks, including custody, counterparty exposure and incident response, according to Stefan Muehlbauer, head of US government affairs at CertiK. “After an incident of this scale, it would be surprising if the Fed and OCC didn’t check in with the banks they supervise,” Muehlbauer told Cointelegraph. “Their mandate is to protect the financial system, and that means understanding where exposures sit and how quickly they can respond.” Banks review security systems after Binance hack According to Reuters, banks have been assessing the hack and checking their systems to figure out whether they could absorb or manage similar threats. Reuters’ report also noted that a cybersecurity team at one of the largest US banks contacted Binance within hours of the hack. A Binance spokesperson confirmed with Cointelegraph that the exchange shared its publicly released incident report with all its banking partners and was not aware of any vulnerabilities affecting them. Muehlbauer explained the procedure currently unfolding is “how a maturing framework should work.” He added that “it’s not a signal that regulators are pulling back from the industry.” The inquiries also come after the Federal Reserve removed a requirement in April 2025 for state member banks to notify regulators before engaging in crypto activities. The Fed said it would continue overseeing those activities through its regular supervisory process. A Federal Reserve spokesperson told Cointelegraph that the agency had nothing to share regarding the reported inquiries. Cointelegraph also contacted the OCC for comment but has not heard back at the time of publishing. Related: Binance traces $6.3B hack to fake job interviews, compromised AI tool The largest crypto hack raises concerns Binance said in its Nov. 3 incident report that approximately $6.34 billion in digital assets were affected by the attack on Oct. 29, with $2.85 billion frozen or intercepted as of the report. According to the crypto exchange, the attack began with compromised software installed by an engineer in June. Hackers later employed social engineering, stolen credentials and malicious software to get access to wallet systems and carry out unauthorized transfers. Dr. Darren Williams, founder and CEO of cybersecurity firm BlackFog, told Cointelegraph that the methods used in the attack pose potential risks to traditional banks, particularly those offering crypto custody and payment services. “Attackers no longer need to break encryption or steal private keys if they can compromise the trusted systems and people authorized to move money,” Williams said. He warned that hackers could use compromised employee devices, accounts or third-party services to move money without triggering any alerts. He also said the growing use of agentic AI in financial operations could pose even more risks. “The priority must be stopping unauthorized transactions and data exfiltration before assets or sensitive information leave the organization, not simply investigating the damage afterwards,” Williams said. Binance has since said that it has strengthened its security controls and was bringing in independent cybersecurity experts to review the attack. Magazine: Binance hackers raced to move billions before it could be frozen

articles.title: Şimşek’ten borç yapılandırması mesajı: Faiz konusunda radikal adım gündemde
articles.summary: Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı Mehmet Şimşek, borç yapılandırması için 705 bin kişinin 531,1 milyar TL’lik borçla başvurduğunu açıkladı. Şimşek, aflara karşı olduğunu belirtirken faiz konusunda radikal bir yaklaşımın değerlendirileceğini söyledi.

articles.titleTr: Şimşek’ten borç yapılandırması mesajı: Faiz konusunda radikal adım gündemde
articles.summaryTr: Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı Mehmet Şimşek, borç yapılandırması için 705 bin kişinin 531,1 milyar TL’lik borçla başvurduğunu açıkladı. Şimşek, aflara karşı olduğunu belirtirken faiz konusunda radikal bir yaklaşımın değerlendirileceğini söyledi.
articles.articleText: Şimşek’ten borç yapılandırması mesajı: Faiz konusunda radikal adım gündemde - Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı Mehmet Şimşek, borç yapılandırması için 705 bin kişinin 531,1 milyar TL’lik borçla başvurduğunu açıkladı. Şimşek, aflara karşı olduğunu belirtirken faiz konusunda radikal bir yaklaşımın değerlendirileceğini söyledi. Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı Mehmet Şimşek, TBMM’deki Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığı bütçe görüşmelerinde milletvekillerinin sorularını yanıtladı. Borç yapılandırmasına yönelik taleplerin hem Cumhur İttifakı’ndan hem de muhalefetten geldiğini belirten Şimşek, faiz oranlarında ve yapılandırma koşullarında yeni bir yaklaşım üzerinde çalışılabileceğinin sinyalini verdi. 705 bin kişi yapılandırma için başvurdu CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Şimşek, borç yapılandırması kapsamında 705 bin kişinin toplam 531,1 milyar TL tutarındaki borcu için başvuru yaptığını açıkladı. Yapılandırmada faizin yüzde 39’a indirildiğini belirten Şimşek, bugüne kadar 31,6 milyar TL tahsilat gerçekleştirildiğini söyledi. “Afları doğru bulmuyorum” Borçların yapılandırılmasına yönelik taleplere değinen Şimşek, vergi ve borç aflarına karşı olduğunu ifade etti. Teminat konusunun büyük ölçüde çözüldüğünü belirten Şimşek, 10 milyon TL’ye kadar teminat aranmadığını ve 72 aya varan vade imkânının bulunduğunu söyledi. Şimşek, geriye faiz konusunun kaldığına dikkat çekti. Faiz konusunda radikal yaklaşım gündemde Şimşek, yapılandırma uygulamasında 72 aylık vadenin etkin biçimde uygulanması gerektiğini belirterek faiz konusunda daha radikal bir yaklaşımın değerlendirilebileceğini söyledi. Şimşek, “72 ayı uygulamada irade koyalım, faiz konusunda radikal bir yaklaşım içine girelim, bu konuyu çalışacağız” ifadelerini kullandı.

articles.articleText: Release Number 9322-26 CFTC Staff Addresses Use of Trust Companies for Daily Settlements November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s Division of Clearing and Risk today issued a no-action letter addressing whether derivatives clearing organizations may use trust companies to conduct daily settlements with clearing members. articles.summaryTr: Borsa İstanbul’da 5 Kasım’da 11 şirket yeni iş ilişkisi, sözleşme, yatırım, varlık satışı ve ihale gelişmelerini duyurdu. Açıklamalarda milyonlarca dolarlık ve milyarlarca liralık işlemler öne çıktı.
articles.articleText: Borsa İstanbul’da 11 şirketten KAP açıklaması: Milyarlık anlaşmalar ve yeni yatırımlar Borsa İstanbul’da 5 Kasım’da 11 şirket yeni iş ilişkisi, sözleşme, yatırım, varlık satışı ve ihale gelişmelerini duyurdu. Açıklamalarda milyonlarca dolarlık ve milyarlarca liralık işlemler öne çıktı. Doğuş Otomotiv (DOAS) – Skoda ile Irak için iş birliği adımı Doğuş Otomotiv, Skoda Auto A.S. ile Irak’ta Skoda markalı binek otomobillerin satış ve satış sonrası servis hizmetlerini üstlenmek amacıyla niyet mektubu imzaladı. Taraflar arasında nihai anlaşmanın yapılması için önemli bir adım atıldı. Doğu Aras Enerji (ARASE) – 500 milyon TL’lik enerji satış anlaşması Şirketin bağlı ortaklığı Aras Elektrik Perakende Satış A.Ş., Kasım 2026 dönemi için toplam 156 bin MWh enerji satış anlaşması yaptı. Anlaşmanın KDV hariç tutarı 500 milyon TL olarak açıklandı. Tutarın piyasa fiyatlarına göre değişebileceği belirtildi. Meka Global (MEKAG) – Suriye’de distribütörlük anlaşması Meka Global’in yüzde 100 bağlı ortaklığı Meka İthalat İhracat Pazarlama ve Ticaret A.Ş., Suriye’de faaliyet gösteren bir şirketle ürün satışına yönelik distribütörlük sözleşmesi imzaladı. Girişim Elektrik (GESAN) – 2,5 milyon dolarlık sözleşme Girişim Elektrik, Kahramanmaraş’ta gerçekleştirilecek Depolamalı Güneş Enerjisi Santrali projesinin enerji iletim hattı yapım işi için yurt içindeki bir müşteriyle 2,5 milyon dolar bedelli sözleşme imzaladı. Alcatel Lucent Teletaş (ALCTL) – 5,9 milyon dolarlık iş emri Alcatel Lucent Teletaş, Türkiye’de yerleşik bir müşteriyle devam eden iş ilişkisi kapsamında 5 milyon 896 bin 30 dolar tutarında iş emri imzaladığını duyurdu. Europower Enerji (EUPWR) – 1,13 milyar TL’lik TEİAŞ sözleşmesi Europower Enerji’nin yüzde 49 oranında ortak olduğu Euroes Teknoloji ve Taahhüt A.Ş., TEİAŞ’ın Konya Kuzey–IGA GES enerji iletim hattı yapım ihalesinde en avantajlı teklifi vermişti. Şirkete iletilen sözleşme davetinin ardından taraflar sözleşmeyi imzaladı. Sözleşmenin baz bedeli 1 milyar 133 milyon 133 bin 133 TL oldu. Anadolu Sigorta (ANSGR) – Brüt prim üretimi yüzde 18,5 arttı Anadolu Sigorta’nın 1 Ocak–31 Ekim 2026 dönemindeki bağımsız denetimden geçmemiş brüt prim üretimi 88 milyar 568 milyon 746 bin 439 TL’ye ulaştı. Böylece brüt prim üretimi geçen yılın aynı dönemine göre yüzde 18,5 artış gösterdi. Hun Yenilenebilir Enerji (HUNER) – Letonya’ya 6 milyon euroluk enerji depolama yatırımı Hun Yenilenebilir Enerji’nin yüzde 60 payını devraldığı Letonya merkezli SW Electricity SIA’nın Riga’da geliştirdiği yaklaşık 15 MW/30 MWh kapasiteli bataryalı enerji depolama projesinin inşaatına 2027 yılında başlanması planlanıyor. Projenin toplam yatırım tutarının yaklaşık 6 milyon euro olması bekleniyor. Finansman için Letonya’daki bankalardan teklifler alınırken kredi koşullarına ilişkin görüşmeler sürüyor. Gelecek Varlık Yönetimi (GLCVY) – 445,7 milyon TL’lik portföy ihalesi Gelecek Varlık Yönetimi, Fibabanka’nın 5 Kasım’da gerçekleştirdiği tahsili gecikmiş alacak satışında, 445,7 milyon TL anapara büyüklüğündeki bireysel portföyün ihalesini kazandı. İhale sonucunun kesinleşmesi için Fibabanka Yönetim Kurulu’nun onayı gerekiyor. Skyalp Finansal Teknolojiler (SKYLP) – 70,4 milyon TL’lik pay devri Skyalp Finansal Teknolojiler, iştiraki Tenk Bilişim Teknolojileri Danışmanlık A.Ş.’de sahip olduğu ve şirket sermayesinin yüzde 3,81’ine karşılık gelen 1 milyon 253 bin 122 adet payı, Hedef Portföy Gelişim Girişim Sermayesi Yatırım Fonu’na devretme kararı aldı. Pay devri için 70 milyon 387 bin TL bedel üzerinden sözleşme imzalandı. Gelirin Borsa Para Piyasası borçlarının ödenmesi ve işletme sermayesinde kullanılması planlanıyor. Deniz Gayrimenkul Yatırım Ortaklığı (DZGYO) – Bodrum’daki otel 979,4 milyon TL’ye satıldı Deniz Gayrimenkul Yatırım Ortaklığı, Bodrum’un Eskiçeşme Mahallesi’nde bulunan otel binasını KDV hariç 979 milyon 364 bin TL bedelle sattı. Gayrimenkulün ekspertiz değeri 968 milyon 700 bin TL olarak açıklanmıştı. Satış bedelinin 13 Kasım 2026 tarihinde tahsil edilmesi bekleniyor.

articles.title: Paraguay’da bankacılık krizi hükümeti devirdi: Devlet Başkanı Pena istifa etti
articles.summary: Paraguay’da yaklaşık 3 milyon müşterinin banka hesaplarına erişimini kaybetmesine yol açan Ueno krizinin ardından siyasi baskılar arttı. Devlet Başkanı Santiago Pena istifa ederken, Meclis’in azil sürecini onayladığı bildirildi.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Paraguay’da bankacılık krizi hükümeti devirdi: Devlet Başkanı Pena istifa etti
articles.summaryTr: Paraguay’da yaklaşık 3 milyon müşterinin banka hesaplarına erişimini kaybetmesine yol açan Ueno krizinin ardından siyasi baskılar arttı. Devlet Başkanı Santiago Pena istifa ederken, Meclis’in azil sürecini onayladığı bildirildi.
articles.articleText: Paraguay’da bankacılık krizi hükümeti devirdi: Devlet Başkanı Pena istifa etti - Paraguay’da yaklaşık 3 milyon müşterinin banka hesaplarına erişimini kaybetmesine yol açan Ueno krizinin ardından siyasi baskılar arttı. Devlet Başkanı Santiago Pena istifa ederken, Meclis’in azil sürecini onayladığı bildirildi. Paraguay’da dijital banka Ueno’nun çöküşüyle başlayan bankacılık krizi, ülkenin siyasi yönetimini de sarstı. Devlet Başkanı Santiago Pena, bankanın faaliyetlerinin durması ve milyonlarca müşterinin hesaplarına erişememesi üzerine artan siyasi baskılar nedeniyle Perşembe günü görevinden istifa etti. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Pena, yayımladığı video mesajında ülkenin istikrarını, toplumsal barışı ve demokratik kurumları koruma gerekliliğini göz önünde bulundurarak istifa kararı aldığını açıkladı. Bloomberg’in haberine göre Paraguay Meclisi, Pena’nın azledilmesini onayladı. İstifanın resmiyet kazanması için Senato’nun da kararı kabul etmesi gerekiyor. Ueno krizi 3 milyon müşteriyi etkiledi Yaklaşık 6,5 milyon nüfuslu Paraguay’da Ueno’nun faaliyetlerinin durdurulması, yaklaşık 3 milyon müşterinin banka hesaplarına erişememesine yol açtı. Ülke nüfusunun neredeyse yarısını etkileyen kriz, hükümet üzerindeki baskıyı artırdı. Paraguay Merkez Bankası, Ueno’nun asgari sermaye yeterliliği koşullarını ihlal ettiğini tespit etmesinin ardından bankaya el koydu. Başlangıçta sınırlı ölçekte faaliyet gösteren bir finansal teknoloji şirketi olan Ueno, hızlı büyümesinin ardından yaklaşık 850 milyon dolarlık kamu fonunu yöneten orta ölçekli bir bankaya dönüşmüştü. Kriz kapsamında Paraguay Merkez Bankası Başkanı da Salı günü istifa etti. Bankanın sekiz yöneticisi ise gözaltına alındı. Pena’ya çıkar çatışması ve usulsüzlük suçlamaları Muhalefet milletvekilleri, Pena’yı Ueno kriziyle bağlantılı olarak çıkar çatışması, emeklilik fonlarının kötüye kullanılması ve kurumsal usulsüzlüklerin örtbas edilmesiyle suçladı. Pena’nın geçmişte Ueno ile iş bağlantılarının bulunması da tartışmaların odağında yer aldı. Protestocular devlet başkanının istifasını talep ederken, muhalefet partileri azil sürecini başlatmak amacıyla Kongre’de olağanüstü oturum çağrısı yaptı. ABD Başkanı Donald Trump’ın müttefiklerinden biri olarak bilinen Pena, kendi muhafazakâr partisinden bazı üyelerin desteğini de kaybetti. Pena, istifa açıklamasında kamu fonlarının ve Paraguay halkına ait kaynakların korunması gerektiğini vurguladı. Ayrıca mevduat garanti fonunun görevini yerine getirmesini ve fonların geri ödenmesinin güvence altına alınmasını istedi. Yeni devlet başkanı Pedro Alliana olacak Pena’nın istifasının Senato tarafından resmen kabul edilmesi bekleniyor. Kongre'nin istifayı görüşmek üzere yerel saatle 14.00'te toplanacağı bildirildi. Devlet Başkan Yardımcısı Pedro Alliana’nın ise yerel saatle 15.30 civarında yemin ederek görevi devralması bekleniyor. Bankacılık krizinin siyasi sonuçlarının yanı sıra Paraguay’ın, özellikle komşusu Brezilya başta olmak üzere yabancı yatırımcılar nezdindeki istikrarlı yatırım merkezi imajına da zarar verdiği değerlendiriliyor.

articles.titleTr: French protests see numbers surge as unions join strikes over high cost of living
articles.summaryTr: The interior ministry estimates 600,000 people joined protests across France, while the unions say the number was far higher.
articles.articleText: French protests see numbers surge as unions join strikes over high cost of living - Published More than 600,000 protesters have taken part in rallies and marches across France, according to France's interior ministry, with five unions joining a day of action demanding more money for wages and public services. The left-wing CGT union put the number of people taking part in Thursday's mobilisation at 1.57 million and hailed the figure as "a level unmatched" since 2023, citing big protests in Paris, Marseille, Bordeaux and Lille. As darkness fell in Paris, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said he would convene a "social conference" with unions and employers next Monday. The wave of protests began in September over poor conditions and resources at lycées (high schools), before spreading to universities, workers and a revived "yellow-vest" movement against high prices. The unions had vowed to take the co-ordinated move against the government "to the next level", and CGT chief Sophie Binet had said their message was that "the only thing that will bring this mobilisation to a halt is responding to our demands". Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez had earlier deployed 70,000 police, vowing "an extremely firm response" to any potential outbreaks of violence. Some unrest was reported in several cities. A car was set alight near the Gallieni bridge over the Rhône river in Lyon, as hundreds of activists from the radical left-wing "black bloc" clashed with police. Clashes were also reported in the north-western city of Rennes, where the local prefect said a "hostile group of masked individuals" had gathered in front of the main union march. Tear gas was used to clear a square in the south-western city of Bordeaux and a teenager was hurt in a stabbing involving a student at a high-school blockade in the Seine-Saint-Denis suburb of northern Paris. But the trouble was not on the scale seen during the last big day of protests, on Saturday 17 October, when more than 2,000 stores were looted and historic buildings set on fire. The provisional numbers reported on Thursday were higher than on 17 October, considered the biggest day of rallies until now when the interior ministry said 550,000 people had turned out and the unions counted 800,000. Earlier on Thursday the leader of the CFDT union, Marylise Léon, said she would be happy if the protests matched that earlier level. A coalition of unions across the public and private sector had urged workers, pensioners and young people to join Thursday's day of strikes to intensify pressure on the government. In particular they are seeking a rise in the minimum wage, or Smic, which is currently €12.31 (£10) an hour. Sophie Binet told reporters at the start of a march in central Paris that protesters had "just reached a new level in their mobilisation" and were demanding immediate answers. An estimated 9.89% of civil servants were taking part in the strikes, according to government figures. Disruption was reported in schools, hospitals and public transport, and the Eiffel Tower and some exhibition rooms at the Louvre museum in Paris had to close. Workers were also asked to halt production at oil refineries and France was expected to import more electricity than it produced on Thursday because of disruption at nuclear plants. The head of the CFDT complained that it was not just the minimum wage that needed to increase. "We are asking for a net increase of €100 a month," Marylise Léon explained. The government has sought to appease public anger over rising prices, bringing down the cost of fuel by releasing 10 million barrels of diesel from strategic reserves. Ministers have also promised school students to reform the unpopular Parcoursup university admissions platform and eventually replace it by 2028. The prime minister said early on Thursday evening that Monday's "social conference" with unions and employers would seek to "provide answers to questions surrounding purchasing power and wages". However, the government by its own admission has little room to manoeuvre, as it looks to make tens of billions of euros in savings, in a bid to cut the budget deficit to 5% of GDP. The education ministry said that 16% of teachers had gone on strike on Thursday, and the unions said disruption had affected more than one in four lycées, which cater for 15-18 year-olds, as well as the vast majority of universities. "Now it's not only about [investing in] public services in education and higher education, it's about all of the public services in France," the vice-president of the Unef student union, Alice De Brito, told the BBC. Meanwhile, a revived gilets jaunes (yellow-vest) movement that staged a revolt against the high cost of living several years ago has called for further blockades and protests on Friday and Saturday too. Thursday's march was eventually allowed in central Paris, although not along the route proposed by the unions between Place de la Bastille and Place de la Concorde, which would have taken protesters near the National Assembly, the Élysée Palace, and the prime minister's residence at Hôtel Matignon. Instead, the march followed another central route from Place de la République to Place de la Nation. The interior minister had earlier spoken of three potential risks on Thursday, from radical left "black blocs" groups and looting to wildcat marches without union authorisation. - Published4 days ago

articles.title: Shares in Musk's SpaceX plunge as tech and AI stocks fall
articles.summary: The market has been reacting to possible tougher scrutiny of data centre construction and the AI industry following the US mid-terms
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Shares in Musk's SpaceX plunge as tech and AI stocks fall
articles.summaryTr: The market has been reacting to possible tougher scrutiny of data centre construction and the AI industry following the US mid-terms
articles.articleText: Shares in Musk's SpaceX plunge as tech and AI stocks fall - Published Shares in Elon Musk's SpaceX have plunged as tech and artificial intelligence stocks more broadly plummeted a day after the Democrats swept to victory in the midterms. Those losses dragged the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite stock index down, which had fallen by more than 5% at one point in early trading. The market has been reacting to possible tougher scrutiny of data centre construction and the artificial intelligence (AI) industry following Democrat wins in key data centre states including Texas. Following the election, some tech leaders have acknowledged they need to improve their communication around data centres and the benefits of AI. SpaceX shares were down more than 9% in by lunchtime in Thursday trading, while Tesla shares dropped more than 11%. Musk had spent nearly $450m backing Republican campaigns, including at least $45m in support of Ken Paxton for the Texas senate seat, but Texas was turned blue in the Democratic tsunami on Tuesday night. Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa campaigned heavily against data centres, pledging a moratorium on new construction in the sector. Shares in chipmakers have been suffering, with AMD dropping more than 14% on Thursday, while Micron shares had dropped by as much as 17% before recovering slightly. Intel shares are down by more than 7% and shares in Nvidia have fallen nearly 9%, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index had fallen by 10%. The stock falls also hit the S&P 500 index, which dropped by 3.8% by lunchtime. Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, said the steep sell-off on the Nasdaq and the S&P 500 was sending shockwaves into other markets. "Fresh panic over the AI trade has hit Wall Street hard," she said. "Fears that the vast sums poured into AI infrastructure may not deliver the returns investors have been banking on are now colliding with the prospect of a sharp slowdown in data centre construction." Some tech leaders have said they were caught off guard by the backlash against data centres in the midterms. OpenAI president and co-founder Greg Brockman said he believed everyone had been surprised by the reaction to data centres, and more work needed to be done to ensure communities were on board. "A lot of our shift over the course of this year has really been to realise that from San Francisco trying to build infrastructure in Texas, Georgia, and other places, you can't just tweet and say: 'This is going to be good.' You need to be in those communities," Brockman said at the WSJ Tech conference in Napa, California on Wednesday evening. Meta's president Dina Powell McCormick agreed that the industry needed to improve their communication about the benefits of AI. "I think we need to double and triple down on telling the story," she told the WSJ conference. Alongside the immediate impacts of the US mid-term elections, some investors have become concerned that AI shares could be in a bubble that is due a correction.

articles.summaryTr: Tofaş, 2026’nın ilk 9 ayında 10,97 milyar TL net kâr açıkladı. Şirketin üçüncü çeyrek kârı 4,33 milyar TL ile analistlerin 2,51 milyar TL’lik medyan beklentisini geride bıraktı.
articles.articleText: Tofaş'tan (TOASO) beklentileri aşan 3.çeyrek bilançosu: İşte detaylar! - Tofaş, 2026’nın ilk 9 ayında 10,97 milyar TL net kâr açıkladı. Şirketin üçüncü çeyrek kârı 4,33 milyar TL ile analistlerin 2,51 milyar TL’lik medyan beklentisini geride bıraktı. Tofaş Türk Otomobil Fabrikası A.Ş. (TOASO), 2026 yılı üçüncü çeyrek finansal sonuçlarını 5 Kasım 2026 tarihinde Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu’nda (KAP) açıkladı. Şirketin hem çeyreklik hem de dokuz aylık kârında güçlü artış kaydedildi. Tofaş’ın net kârı 9 ayda yüzde 189 arttı CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Tofaş, 1 Ocak–30 Eylül 2026 döneminde toplam 10 milyar 972 milyon 737 bin TL net kâr elde etti. Şirket, 2025’in aynı döneminde 3 milyar 802 milyon 128 bin TL kâr açıklamıştı. Böylece net kâr yıllık bazda yüzde 189 arttı. Şirketin 2026 yılının üçüncü çeyreğindeki net kârı ise 4 milyar 331 milyon 820 bin TL oldu. Satış gelirleri yüzde 21 yükseldi Tofaş’ın satış gelirleri, 2026’nın ilk dokuz ayında geçen yılın aynı dönemine göre yüzde 21 artarak 293 milyar 540 milyon 755 bin TL’ye ulaştı. 2025’in ilk dokuz ayında satışlar 245 milyar 788 milyon 653 bin TL seviyesindeydi. Esas faaliyet kârı da geçen yılın aynı dönemindeki 625 milyon 350 bin TL’lik zarardan 2026’nın ilk dokuz ayında 5 milyar 552 milyon 458 bin TL kâra döndü. Şirketin FAVÖK’ü ise 6 milyar 723 milyon 350 bin TL’den 7 milyar 533 milyon 739 bin TL’ye yükseldi. Tofaş’ın varlıkları ve özkaynakları 30 Eylül 2026 itibarıyla Tofaş’ın toplam varlıkları 212 milyar 199 milyon 178 bin TL oldu. Şirketin toplam borçları 139 milyar 418 milyon 250 bin TL, özkaynakları ise 72 milyar 780 milyon 928 bin TL olarak kaydedildi. Şirketin piyasa değeri 111,80 milyar TL seviyesinde bulunurken F/K oranı 6,37, PD/DD oranı 1,54 olarak açıklandı. Tofaş bilançosu beklentileri aştı Matriks Haber tarafından gerçekleştirilen bilanço anketine 12 aracı kurum katıldı. Ankete göre Tofaş’ın 2026 üçüncü çeyrek net kârı için ortalama beklenti 2 milyar 507 milyon 100 bin TL, medyan beklenti ise 2 milyar 513 milyon TL oldu. Şirketin açıkladığı 4 milyar 331 milyon 820 bin TL’lik net kâr, hem ortalama hem de medyan beklentinin belirgin şekilde üzerinde gerçekleşti. Böylece Tofaş, üçüncü çeyrek bilançosuyla analist beklentilerini aştı.

articles.titleTr: Paraguay President Santiago Peña resigns after bank collapse
articles.summaryTr: The move follows a bank collapse and after the lower house of congress voted in favour of pursuing an impeachment trial against him.
articles.articleText: Paraguay President Santiago Peña resigns after bank collapse - Published Paraguay's President Santiago Peña has announced his resignation following a political crisis sparked by the collapse of a bank linked to him. "I want to apologise to the people if at any point I failed," he said in a video message on social media. "It was never my intention to betray the trust you placed in me." The crisis erupted after Ueno Bank entered an insolvency process, which froze all operations. Lawmakers accused Peña, who was a shareholder until last year in the company that owned the bank, of conflicts of interest and misconduct. Peña has rejected suggestions of impropriety. His resignation comes after Paraguay's lower house of congress voted in favour of pursuing an impeachment trial. In his video message posted on X, Peña said his resignation was to protect stability, social peace and democratic institutions. Ueno Bank has said it has about three million customers, equivalent to about 60% of Paraguay's adult population. It held pensions and some other public funds and, after its collapse earlier this week, millions could not access their accounts. The central bank seized the digital lender, and people took to the streets protesting and demanding Peña's resignation. A new president of the Central Bank of Paraguay has been appointed and Congress has approved a process to pay depositors. Peña won election in 2023 representing Paraguay's ruling conservative Colorado Party, beating a centre-left challenger.

articles.titleTr: Paraguay president resigns after collapse of Ueno digital bank
articles.summaryTr: Santiago Peña stepped down amid mounting scrutiny over his former ties to Ueno Bank’s parent company, as the lender’s collapse left millions of customers unable to access their funds.
articles.articleText: Paraguay president resigns after collapse of Ueno digital bank Santiago Peña stepped down amid mounting scrutiny over his former ties to Ueno Bank’s parent company, as the lender’s collapse left millions of customers unable to access their funds. Paraguayan President Santiago Peña announced his resignation Thursday amid a deepening political crisis triggered by the collapse of digital lender Ueno Bank. In a video posted to X, Peña said he was stepping down to preserve the country’s stability, social peace and democratic institutions. He added that his priority was protecting Paraguayans who had entrusted their savings to the financial system. Paraguay’s central bank announced resolution proceedings for Ueno Bank on Tuesday after finding that its solvency ratio had fallen below half of the regulatory minimum. Peña faced mounting political scrutiny over his former business ties to Grupo Vázquez, the conglomerate that controls Ueno Bank. He remained a business partner of the group until March 2025, according to AP. Peña has denied any wrongdoing, arguing that the controversy began as a regulatory matter before escalating into a political dispute. The banking crisis also coincided with elevated asking prices for Tether’s USDt on Bybit’s Paraguay-facing peer-to-peer marketplace. One listing viewed early Thursday offered USDt at 6,942 Paraguayan guaraníes, approximately 13% above the central bank’s Nov. 4 reference rate of 6,144.02 guaraníes per US dollar. His resignation came as lawmakers debated impeachment proceedings over alleged conflicts of interest, misuse of pension funds and institutional cover-ups linked to Ueno Bank’s collapse, according to Reuters. Peña, who was elected in April 2023 and took office that August, was serving a five-year term scheduled to end in 2028. Under Paraguay’s Constitution, Vice President Pedro Alliana would succeed him for the remainder of the term if Congress accepts his resignation. Ueno Bank’s collapse affects millions of customers Ueno Bank had grown rapidly since 2021 into one of Paraguay’s largest financial institutions, serving more than 3 million customers in a country of roughly 6.5 million people. Ueno first came under regulatory scrutiny in June over loans to companies linked to its controlling shareholder, Grupo Vázquez. In an October statement, the bank acknowledged receiving regulatory notices on June 5 and July 24 requiring adjustments to its related-party lending exposure. On Nov. 2, the Central Bank of Paraguay initiated resolution proceedings after adjustments to the bank’s financial statements pushed its solvency ratio below half the regulatory minimum. Authorities suspended the bank’s operations, restricting customers’ access to their deposits. Paraguayan authorities detained eight Ueno Bank executives on Nov. 3, including Grupo Vázquez president Miguel Vázquez and bank president Juan Manuel Gustale, according to local newspaper ABC Color. A court subsequently ordered six executives held in pretrial detention and placed two others under house arrest. Paraguay begins depositor payouts amid protests On Thursday, Paraguay’s central bank announced that it would start deposit guarantee payments to eligible clients with balances of up to 10 million guaraníes (about $1,630), provided they had no outstanding debts to Ueno and held accounts at other financial institutions. Under the country’s deposit insurance system, deposits are protected up to 228.3 million guaraníes (about $37,200) per depositor, per financial institution. The bank’s collapse sparked protests in the nation’s capital, Asunción, where hundreds of depositors, pensioners and workers demanded the return of their savings and accountability from government officials. This is a developing story. We will update this article as more information becomes available.

articles.title: Hoax bomb threats target European airlines and airports for second time in a week
articles.summary: At least 21 flights across Europe are affected in what the UK government calls a "malicious hoax threat".

articles.titleTr: Hoax bomb threats target European airlines and airports for second time in a week
articles.summaryTr: At least 21 flights across Europe are affected in what the UK government calls a "malicious hoax threat".
articles.articleText: Hoax bomb threats target European airlines and airports for second time in a week - Published At least 21 aircraft and several airports across Europe have been targeted by bomb threats in the second such incident this week, with the UK calling it a "malicious hoax". Flights to Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, France, Italy, Poland and Romania were affected. An Aer Lingus plane from Dublin to Rome was diverted to an air base in France and Italian fighter jets escorted Finnair's Helsinki-Rome flight. EasyJet said its flights from Newcastle and Glasgow were met by police in Prague as a precaution. London Heathrow and Birmingham airports received threats that were assessed as not credible. No explosives have been found during searches, and it is not clear if the incidents, some claimed by a little known group, are related. - Who could be behind hoax bomb threats to European air travel? - Published50 minutes ago The airport authorities in Italy's capital Rome said the hoax threat against two inbound flights received on Thursday had come by email. The warnings were signed on behalf of a group or individual calling themselves "Fighters of the Male State", claiming to be targeting a "feminist regime" and wanting to "make our mark on history". They threatened to "turn the skies red" with explosions. These details were first reported by Italian media and then confirmed to the BBC by Aeroporti di Roma, which manages both of the city airports. "Fighters of the Male State" likely refers to the Russian group "Muzhskoi Legion" ( "Male Legion") - an ultra-right group with such extreme views it was banned by a Moscow court in 2021. Yet it retained tens of thousands of online followers as it cheered on the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine in the following year. But that email, even if genuine, is unlikely to provide the leads that police and airport authorities need to pin down who is generating these hoaxes and why. UK Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander described Thursday's incidents as "malicious hoax threats." She said the government was taking "these threats seriously", stressing that there were "established processes for dealing with hoax and malicious threats". A UK government spokesperson later said the threats reported "in the early hours" of the day had been "resolved", without giving any further details. Heathrow later said in a statement it had received a threat earlier in the day which was "deemed not credible", adding there was "no risk to passengers, colleagues or the aircraft". "There are robust UK aviation security standards in place to assess and safely manage these types of situations," the statement said. Meanwhile, a Birmingham Airport spokesperson told the BBC it had received a threat, after which "processes were immediately initiated in conjunction with emergency services and partners". The following flights were targeted by threats on Thursday: - Aer Lingus said its flight from Dublin to Rome diverted to Normandy, landing safely. The company added that it was working to "re-accommodate customers to their final destination as soon as possible". - Two Finnair flights from Helsinki landed at their destinations as normal, the airline said. One was escorted into Rome's Fiumicino airport by Italian Air Force fighter jets, Aeroporti di Roma told the BBC, while the other landed in Vienna, Austria - Wizz Air said two flights which departed Milan were affected - one was heading to Warsaw, before being diverting to Vienna; the other landed safely in Bucharest, with teams inspecting the aircraft - Polish airline LOT said its flight from Warsaw to Brussels landed as planned, and "no suspicious items were found". Another LOT flight from Warsaw to Paris was stopped before take-off and the plane and baggage underwent a security screening, with no hazardous items found - Three Ryanair flights landed in Bulgaria, according to Bulgarian media - one from Copenhagen and another from Madrid landed in the capital Sofia, while a third coming from London bound for Sofia landed in Plovdiv. The flights were escorted by Bulgarian air force fighter jets - No explosives were found on four flights which landed in Prague, Czech police said. EasyJet later said its flights from Newcastle and Glasgow were among those affected. "Passengers on both flights disembarked normally," the company said - Aegean Airlines said it "was informed of a bomb threat" concerning two of its flights from Thessaloniki in Greece to Milan, and also from Athens to Vienna. It said threat was "unfounded", and both flights departed from the respective airports" - A Ryanair flight from Porto in Portugal landed safely in Milan as planned, with bomb disposal experts checking them on arrival, Italy's Ansa news agency reported - Spain's airport authority said it had received bomb threats affecting three flights at Madrid airport, but any threat was ruled out following inspections. Iberia later said two of its flights - Milan-Madrid and Rome-Madrid - were affected. It was not clear whether the third plane was the above reported Ryanair Madrid to Sofia flight - Air Serbia said its flight from Belgrade to Bucharest "landed safely at its destination airport", and after checks, a reported bomb threat was "assessed as unfounded" Emily Noble, who was aboard the diverted Aer Lingus plane from Dublin to Rome, said she was about an hour into her flight to attend a friend's wedding in the Italian capital when passengers were told about a "technical" problem. Later, as the Aer Lingus plane began circling for an unplanned landing in France, the pilot said there was a "security" issue, the 26-year-old from Dublin told BBC Verify. On board it was "an odd experience," Noble said. "It was worrying because we didn't know what was going on, but we were all trying to be as calm as we could." Noble says she could hear fighter jets during the landing and saw one touch down behind the aircraft. After landing at the Évreux-Fauville air base in Normandy, passengers learned the flight had been the subject of a bomb threat. Noble said they remained on board for two-and-a-half hours while police and military personnel carried out checks, including searches with sniffer dogs. The passengers were later told they would be taken to an airport in Paris and another plane would fly them on to Rome. Philip Baum, professor of aviation security at the University of Coventry, said the industry "faces multiple bomb threats every single day" but he had been "surprised" by this week's incidents. A flight is diverted "only when the threat is credible and the authorities believe there is a potential of explosive device on board", he said. He said the concern was that "if you issue enough hoax threats, then complacency could set in and a real threat could be ignored - or they could be a diversion". Marco Chan, an aviation expert at Kingston University, told the BBC the threats were "most likely a hoax, but the system is right to treat it as real". He said they were being viewed by some experts as "possibly part of a pattern of cheap, deniable disruption" to air travel. Hoaxes can also come from copycats, he said, but "three days of incidents is too small a sample to separate coordination from contagion". Two days ago, seven European flights, including two from the UK, were searched after bomb threats were made. No explosives were found on any of the planes after searches. On Monday, a Wizz Air flight travelling from London Luton Airport to Sofia was escorted by a Hungarian fighter jet to Budapest after a mid-air bomb threat. articles.title: Interest rates hiked to 4% in first increase in over three years
articles.summary: Most analysts expected the increase from 3.75% to 4%.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Interest rates hiked to 4% in first increase in over three years
articles.summaryTr: Most analysts expected the increase from 3.75% to 4%.
articles.articleText: Interest rates hiked to 4% in first increase in over three years - Published Interest rates have risen for the first time in more than three years and the Bank of England has signalled a further increase is likely unless the US-Iran war is resolved. Rates rose to 4% from 3.75% in a bid to curb inflation mainly driven by the conflict's impact on global oil prices. Andrew Bailey, the Bank's governor, said the decision "shouldn't be seen as the first in an inevitable long sequence of hikes", but warned "unless the conflict in the Middle East is resolved, neither does it seem likely to be the last increase". The higher level will increase the cost of borrowing for things such as mortgages, loans and credit cards, but will also lead to higher returns on savings. The Bank's rate-setting committee all backed increasing interest rates, with eight out of nine voting in favour of the rise to 4%. One member wanted an even bigger increase to 4.25%. Bailey said the hike was warranted due to higher energy prices and pointed to what happens in the Middle East as the main factor in future decisions. "Put simply, it requires real progress towards settling the conflict in the Middle East," the governor said. Bailey said he could "see the argument" for a further rate hike, before taking a "more conditional approach" dependent on the path of energy prices and inflation in the coming months. However, the views of members on the rate-setting committee differed on the path forward. Clare Lombardelli agreed there was "likely to be a case for a further increase in rates in the near term", while Megan Greene went further, suggesting "additional hikes" might be likely depending on how inflation impacted wages, prices and the jobs market. However, Alan Taylor said the rate rise was a "a risk-management 'one-for-now' insurance hike". Inflation, which measures the pace of price rises over time, is well below its peak of a few years ago but remains above the Bank of England's 2% target and is expected to increase further next year. Prices rose 3.5% in the year to September 2026, largely due to higher fuel prices. Millions of households are also set to be hit by energy bill increases in January. Higher fuel prices can lead to prices rising for a host of goods and staples as businesses pass on higher costs to customers. But the Bank said there was "limited evidence" this had happened so far for goods, such as food, with some firms absorbing cost increases and accepting lower margins. In an interview with the BBC, Bailey defended the decision to raise rates despite the Bank's assessment that inflation was yet to spread to other parts of the economy. He said further increases in energy prices are putting upward pressure on inflation and "that's what we have to seek to lean against". Patrick Bryson, from Brighton, is set to see his five-year mortgage term with a 3.51% interest rate end soon. The best deal the 51-year-old can find is a 5.17% loan with HSBC, which means his repayments will jump from £1,420 to £1,680 a month from February. "The only thing that bugs me about the mortgage is that after five years of paying it off we are now paying more than we were before," said the father-of-three. "That's a bit of a slap in the face." The guitar teacher, who has a combined income of around £68,000 a year with his wife, who manages a care home, said the couple is feeling pressure on their finances and so have changed their shopping habits and are looking to reduce their subcription outgoings. "Over the last year I have stopped buying wine, we don't go out to eat much anymore, we have knocked takeaways on the head. The prices are ridiculous," he said. - Three ways the interest rate rise could affect you - Published7 hours ago - Faisal Islam: How high will interest rates go? - Published7 hours ago The Bank now expects inflation to peak at 4.9% in the middle of next year, higher than it originally estimated, and not return to 2% until 2028. But in an "adverse scenario", where the US-Iran war could escalate further and send oil prices higher, inflation could reach 6.2% in 2027, it suggested. While the UK cannot control global energy prices, the Bank raised rates, for the first time since August 2023, in order to limit the knock-on effects of high energy prices resulting in inflation going up across the board. Its base rate is what it charges other banks and building societies to borrow money, which influences what customers for mortgages, loans, credit cards get charged, as well as savings rates. The rate rise will see 510,000 tracker mortgage-holders see a £31 monthly jump in repayments, according to banking trade body UK Finance. Homeowners on fixed deals will see no change, though future products may be affected. However, people on variable deals will be impacted depending on how their lender reacts to the rate rise. Typically a 0.25pp rise means a £14 increase per month in repayments. Get in touch Do you have a mortgage, a credit card, a car finance agreement? "Put simply, it requires real progress towards settling the conflict in the Middle East," the governor said. Bailey said he could "see the argument" for a further rate hike, before taking a "more conditional approach" dependent on the path of energy prices and inflation in the coming months. However, the views of members on the rate-setting committee differed on the path forward. Clare Lombardelli agreed there was "likely to be a case for a further increase in rates in the near term", while Megan Greene went further, suggesting "additional hikes" might be likely depending on how inflation impacted wages, prices and the jobs market. However, Alan Taylor said the rate rise was a "a risk-management 'one-for-now' insurance hike". Inflation, which measures the pace of price rises over time, is well below its peak of a few years ago but remains above the Bank of England's 2% target and is expected to increase further next year. Prices rose 3.5% in the year to September 2026, largely due to higher fuel prices. Millions of households are also set to be hit by energy bill increases in January. Higher fuel prices can lead to prices rising for a host of goods and staples as businesses pass on higher costs to customers. But the Bank said there was "limited evidence" this had happened so far for goods, such as food, with some firms absorbing cost increases and accepting lower margins. In an interview with the BBC, Bailey defended the decision to raise rates despite the Bank's assessment that inflation was yet to spread to other parts of the economy. He said further increases in energy prices are putting upward pressure on inflation and "that's what we have to seek to lean against". Patrick Bryson, from Brighton, is set to see his five-year mortgage term with a 3.51% interest rate end soon. The best deal the 51-year-old can find is a 5.17% loan with HSBC, which means his repayments will jump from £1,420 to £1,680 a month from February. "The only thing that bugs me about the mortgage is that after five years of paying it off we are now paying more than we were before," said the father-of-three. "That's a bit of a slap in the face." The guitar teacher, who has a combined income of around £68,000 a year with his wife, who manages a care home, said the couple is feeling pressure on their finances and so have changed their shopping habits and are looking to reduce their subcription outgoings. "Over the last year I have stopped buying wine, we don't go out to eat much anymore, we have knocked takeaways on the head. The prices are ridiculous," he said. - Three ways the interest rate rise could affect you - Published7 hours ago - Faisal Islam: How high will interest rates go? - Published7 hours ago The Bank now expects inflation to peak at 4.9% in the middle of next year, higher than it originally estimated, and not return to 2% until 2028. But in an "adverse scenario", where the US-Iran war could escalate further and send oil prices higher, inflation could reach 6.2% in 2027, it suggested. While the UK cannot control global energy prices, the Bank raised rates, for the first time since August 2023, in order to limit the knock-on effects of high energy prices resulting in inflation going up across the board. Its base rate is what it charges other banks and building societies to borrow money, which influences what customers for mortgages, loans, credit cards get charged, as well as savings rates. The rate rise will see 510,000 tracker mortgage-holders see a £31 monthly jump in repayments, according to banking trade body UK Finance. Homeowners on fixed deals will see no change, though future products may be affected. However, people on variable deals will be impacted depending on how their lender reacts to the rate rise. Typically a 0.25pp rise means a £14 increase per month in repayments. Get in touch Do you have a mortgage, a credit card, a car finance agreement?
