items.articleText: Bakan Mehmet Şimşek'ten fon soruşturmasında dikkat çeken çıkış: Listeler açıklansın - Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı Mehmet Şimşek, fon soruşturmasında listelerin açıklanmasını şahsen istediğini belirtti. Şimşek, bilgiye dayalı çıkışların tespit edilmesi halinde suç duyurusunda bulunulduğunu ve soruşturmada kimseye taviz verilmeyeceğini söyledi. Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı Mehmet Şimşek, Türkiye Büyük Millet Meclisi'nde (TBMM) milletvekillerinin sorularını yanıtladı. Şimşek, sermaye piyasalarında yaşanan gelişmeler, fon soruşturması, Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu'nun (SPK) yetkileri ve Mali Suçları Araştırma Kurulu'nun (MASAK) süreçteki rolüne ilişkin açıklamalarda bulundu. "Listelerin açıklanmasını şahsen isterim" CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Fon soruşturması kapsamında gerçekleştirilen çıkışlara ilişkin değerlendirmelerde bulunan Şimşek, çıkışların bilgiye dayandığının belirlenmesi halinde ilgililer hakkında suç duyurusunda bulunduklarını söyledi. Listelerin kamuoyuyla paylaşılmasına ilişkin de konuşan Şimşek, "Listelerin açıklanmasında engel yok, ben şahsen açıklanmasını isterim." ifadelerini kullandı. "Hazine'nin 1 kuruşu tasfiyede kullanılmadı" Fonların tasfiye sürecine ilişkin açıklamalarda bulunan Şimşek, tasfiye işlemlerinde Hazine kaynaklarının kullanılmadığını belirtti. Şimşek, "Hazine'nin 1 kuruşu tasfiyede kullanılmadı." dedi. "İhmali ve suistimali olan varsa hesap verecektir" Fon soruşturmasında ihmali veya suistimali bulunanların hesap vereceğini belirten Şimşek, "Bu süreçte ihmali ve suistimali olan varsa hesap verecektir. Vermeye başladılar." ifadelerini kullandı. Daha önce görev yapan SPK başkanlarıyla ilgili soruşturma başlatıldığını aktaran Şimşek, önceki başkan hakkında soruşturma izni verildiğini söyledi. Şimşek, fon soruşturmasında kim olursa olsun hiçbir şekilde taviz verilmeyeceğini vurguladı. SPK'nın yetkilerine ilişkin açıklama Sermaye piyasalarında inceleme ve yaptırım yetkisinin SPK'ya verildiğini belirten Şimşek, bakanın şahsen bu alanlarda piyasaya doğrudan müdahale etme veya düzenleme yapma yetkisinin bulunmadığını ifade etti. Risklerin gündemlerine gelmesinden itibaren ellerindeki bütün araçları kullandıklarını söyleyen Şimşek, 4 Kasım'da kamuoyunu ve ilgili paydaşları uyardıklarını, ancak uyarmakla yetinmediklerini belirtti. MASAK'ın rolüne ilişkin değerlendirme MASAK'ın süreçteki rolüne ilişkin çok sayıda soru yöneltildiğini belirten Şimşek, Türkiye'de sermaye hareketlerinin serbest olduğunu ve MASAK'ın işlemler gerçekleşmeden müdahale edemeyeceğini söyledi. Fonların temerrüde düşmesi ve tasfiye kararı alınmasının ardından MASAK'ın işlem erteleme sürecini kendisinin paylaştığını belirten Şimşek, şüpheli işlem bildirimi bulunmaması durumunda MASAK'ın devreye girmesinin işin doğasına aykırı olduğunu ifade etti. 401 milyar liralık hareketin dörtte üçü fon içi işlem Fonlardan 401 milyar lira çekilip çekilmediğine ilişkin soruya da yanıt veren Şimşek, söz konusu tutarın dörtte üçünün yatırımcı çıkışı olmadığını, fon içi hareketlerden oluştuğunu belirtti. Fonların kuruluşundan tasfiyesine kadar gerçekleştirilen bütün işlemlerin incelendiğini söyleyen Şimşek, kapalı oldukları dönemler dahil tüm işlemlerin kayıt altında bulunduğunu ifade etti. Sorumluların mal varlıklarına tedbir uygulanıyor Savcılık ve ilgili kurumların araştırma ve incelemelerini sürdürdüğünü belirten Şimşek, sorumluların mal varlıklarına tedbir konulduğunu ve bunların Tasarruf Mevduatı Sigorta Fonu'nun (TMSF) geri kazanım hesabına devredildiğini söyledi. "Ara ödemelerden stopaj kesintisi yapılmadı" Fonların tasfiye sürecinde yapılan ödemelerden stopaj kesildiği yönündeki iddialara da yanıt veren Şimşek, böyle bir durumun söz konusu olmadığını belirtti. Ara ödemelerden tevkifat yapılmadığını ifade eden Şimşek, normal tasfiye sürecinde para piyasası fonlarında nemalar dahil tüm ödemelerin gerçekleştirildiğini söyledi. "Piyasaların daha sağlıklı bir yapıya kavuşacağına inanıyoruz" Sermaye piyasalarındaki gelişmelerin servet kanalı üzerindeki etkisine de değinen Şimşek, bu etkiyi küçümsemediklerini belirtti. Şimşek, piyasaların daha sağlıklı bir yapıya kavuşacağına ve yatırımların geleceğine inandıklarını ifade etti.

items.title: Fed, OCC check US banks after Binance hack as experts flag security risks
items.summary: US regulators reportedly contacted banks following last week’s $6.3 billion Binance security hack, while experts raised concerns about transaction security and crypto risks.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Fed, OCC check US banks after Binance hack as experts flag security risks
items.summaryTr: US regulators reportedly contacted banks following last week’s $6.3 billion Binance security hack, while experts raised concerns about transaction security and crypto risks.
items.articleText: Fed, OCC check US banks after Binance hack as experts flag security risks US regulators reportedly contacted banks following last week’s $6.3 billion Binance security hack, while experts raised concerns about transaction security and crypto risks. US regulators reportedly contacted banks following last week’s $6.3 billion Binance hack, as cybersecurity experts raised concerns about how financial institutions handle crypto-related security risks. Officials from the Federal Reserve and Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) began contacting banks on Monday to ask about “unusual activity” or service disruptions, Reuters reported Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter. The reported inquiries could be followed by closer attention to how banks manage crypto-related risks, including custody, counterparty exposure and incident response, according to Stefan Muehlbauer, head of US government affairs at CertiK. “After an incident of this scale, it would be surprising if the Fed and OCC didn’t check in with the banks they supervise,” Muehlbauer told Cointelegraph. “Their mandate is to protect the financial system, and that means understanding where exposures sit and how quickly they can respond.” Banks review security systems after Binance hack According to Reuters, banks have been assessing the hack and checking their systems to figure out whether they could absorb or manage similar threats. Reuters’ report also noted that a cybersecurity team at one of the largest US banks contacted Binance within hours of the hack. A Binance spokesperson confirmed with Cointelegraph that the exchange shared its publicly released incident report with all its banking partners and was not aware of any vulnerabilities affecting them. Muehlbauer explained the procedure currently unfolding is “how a maturing framework should work.” He added that “it’s not a signal that regulators are pulling back from the industry.” The inquiries also come after the Federal Reserve removed a requirement in April 2025 for state member banks to notify regulators before engaging in crypto activities. The Fed said it would continue overseeing those activities through its regular supervisory process. A Federal Reserve spokesperson told Cointelegraph that the agency had nothing to share regarding the reported inquiries. Cointelegraph also contacted the OCC for comment but has not heard back at the time of publishing. Related: Binance traces $6.3B hack to fake job interviews, compromised AI tool The largest crypto hack raises concerns Binance said in its Nov. 3 incident report that approximately $6.34 billion in digital assets were affected by the attack on Oct. 29, with $2.85 billion frozen or intercepted as of the report. According to the crypto exchange, the attack began with compromised software installed by an engineer in June. Hackers later employed social engineering, stolen credentials and malicious software to get access to wallet systems and carry out unauthorized transfers. Dr. Darren Williams, founder and CEO of cybersecurity firm BlackFog, told Cointelegraph that the methods used in the attack pose potential risks to traditional banks, particularly those offering crypto custody and payment services. “Attackers no longer need to break encryption or steal private keys if they can compromise the trusted systems and people authorized to move money,” Williams said. He warned that hackers could use compromised employee devices, accounts or third-party services to move money without triggering any alerts. He also said the growing use of agentic AI in financial operations could pose even more risks. “The priority must be stopping unauthorized transactions and data exfiltration before assets or sensitive information leave the organization, not simply investigating the damage afterwards,” Williams said. Binance has since said that it has strengthened its security controls and was bringing in independent cybersecurity experts to review the attack. Magazine: Binance hackers raced to move billions before it could be frozen

items.title: Şimşek’ten borç yapılandırması mesajı: Faiz konusunda radikal adım gündemde
items.summary: Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı Mehmet Şimşek, borç yapılandırması için 705 bin kişinin 531,1 milyar TL’lik borçla başvurduğunu açıkladı. Şimşek, aflara karşı olduğunu belirtirken faiz konusunda radikal bir yaklaşımın değerlendirileceğini söyledi.

items.summaryTr: Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı Mehmet Şimşek, borç yapılandırması için 705 bin kişinin 531,1 milyar TL’lik borçla başvurduğunu açıkladı. Şimşek, aflara karşı olduğunu belirtirken faiz konusunda radikal bir yaklaşımın değerlendirileceğini söyledi.
items.articleText: Şimşek’ten borç yapılandırması mesajı: Faiz konusunda radikal adım gündemde - Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı Mehmet Şimşek, borç yapılandırması için 705 bin kişinin 531,1 milyar TL’lik borçla başvurduğunu açıkladı. Şimşek, aflara karşı olduğunu belirtirken faiz konusunda radikal bir yaklaşımın değerlendirileceğini söyledi. Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı Mehmet Şimşek, TBMM’deki Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığı bütçe görüşmelerinde milletvekillerinin sorularını yanıtladı. Borç yapılandırmasına yönelik taleplerin hem Cumhur İttifakı’ndan hem de muhalefetten geldiğini belirten Şimşek, faiz oranlarında ve yapılandırma koşullarında yeni bir yaklaşım üzerinde çalışılabileceğinin sinyalini verdi. 705 bin kişi yapılandırma için başvurdu CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Şimşek, borç yapılandırması kapsamında 705 bin kişinin toplam 531,1 milyar TL tutarındaki borcu için başvuru yaptığını açıkladı. Yapılandırmada faizin yüzde 39’a indirildiğini belirten Şimşek, bugüne kadar 31,6 milyar TL tahsilat gerçekleştirildiğini söyledi. “Afları doğru bulmuyorum” Borçların yapılandırılmasına yönelik taleplere değinen Şimşek, vergi ve borç aflarına karşı olduğunu ifade etti. Teminat konusunun büyük ölçüde çözüldüğünü belirten Şimşek, 10 milyon TL’ye kadar teminat aranmadığını ve 72 aya varan vade imkânının bulunduğunu söyledi. Şimşek, geriye faiz konusunun kaldığına dikkat çekti. Faiz konusunda radikal yaklaşım gündemde Şimşek, yapılandırma uygulamasında 72 aylık vadenin etkin biçimde uygulanması gerektiğini belirterek faiz konusunda daha radikal bir yaklaşımın değerlendirilebileceğini söyledi. Şimşek, “72 ayı uygulamada irade koyalım, faiz konusunda radikal bir yaklaşım içine girelim, bu konuyu çalışacağız” ifadelerini kullandı.

Şimşek, “72 ayı uygulamada irade koyalım, faiz konusunda radikal bir yaklaşım içine girelim, bu konuyu çalışacağız” ifadelerini kullandı.

items.articleText: Bakan Şimşek’ten emekliler için yeni düzenleme mesajı: Yaş ve prim günü vurgusu! - Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı Mehmet Şimşek, emeklilerin alım gücünü artırmaya yönelik teknik bir çalışma yürütüldüğünü açıkladı. Düzenlemenin tüm emeklileri kapsayacağını belirten Şimşek, nihai çalışmanın aralık ayında tamamlanmasının beklendiğini söyledi. Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı Mehmet Şimşek, emeklilerin alım gücünü artırmaya yönelik yeni bir düzenleme üzerinde çalışıldığını açıkladı. Şimşek, çalışmanın bütün emeklileri kapsayacağını ve emekliler arasındaki farklılaşmanın yaş ve prim gün sayısına göre yapılmasının daha adil olacağını ifade etti. “Emeklileri yük olarak gören bir cümle kurmadım” CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Emeklilerin yük olarak görüldüğü yönündeki ifadeleri kabul etmediğini belirten Şimşek, “Emeklileri yük diye tarif eden bir cümle kurmadım, kurmam. Emeklilerimizin, emekçilerimizin en büyük düşmanı enflasyondur” dedi. Şimşek, enflasyon düştükçe bunun alım gücüne yansıyacağını ve sabit gelirlileri korumanın yolunun bu olduğunu söyledi. Düzenleme bütün emeklileri kapsayacak Emeklilerin alım gücünü artırmaya yönelik teknik bir çalışma bulunduğunu açıklayan Şimşek, düzenlemenin tüm emeklileri kapsayacağını belirtti. Şimşek, emekliler arasında yaş ve prim gün sayısına göre farklılaşma yapılmasının daha doğru ve adaletli olacağını ifade etti. Nihai çalışma aralık ayında tamamlanacak Çalışmanın birçok bakanlığı ilgilendirdiğini belirten Şimşek, henüz rakam açıklamanın doğru olmayacağını söyledi. Nihai çalışmanın aralık ayı içinde yapılacağını kaydeden Şimşek, düzenlemenin büyük ihtimalle bütçe görüşmelerinin hemen ardından Meclis’in takdirine sunulacağını belirtti.

items.title: CFTC Staff Addresses Use of Trust Companies for Daily Settlements
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC Staff Addresses Use of Trust Companies for Daily Settlements
items.articleText: Release Number 9322-26 CFTC Staff Addresses Use of Trust Companies for Daily Settlements November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s Division of Clearing and Risk today issued a no-action letter addressing whether derivatives clearing organizations may use trust companies to conduct daily settlements with clearing members. According to the letter, a derivatives clearing organization may use a trust company for daily settlements if it treats the trust company as it would a settlement bank under applicable CFTC requirements. -CFTC-

items.articleText: Borsa İstanbul’da 11 şirketten KAP açıklaması: Milyarlık anlaşmalar ve yeni yatırımlar Borsa İstanbul’da 5 Kasım’da 11 şirket yeni iş ilişkisi, sözleşme, yatırım, varlık satışı ve ihale gelişmelerini duyurdu. Açıklamalarda milyonlarca dolarlık ve milyarlarca liralık işlemler öne çıktı. Doğuş Otomotiv (DOAS) – Skoda ile Irak için iş birliği adımı Doğuş Otomotiv, Skoda Auto A.S. ile Irak’ta Skoda markalı binek otomobillerin satış ve satış sonrası servis hizmetlerini üstlenmek amacıyla niyet mektubu imzaladı. Taraflar arasında nihai anlaşmanın yapılması için önemli bir adım atıldı. Doğu Aras Enerji (ARASE) – 500 milyon TL’lik enerji satış anlaşması Şirketin bağlı ortaklığı Aras Elektrik Perakende Satış A.Ş., Kasım 2026 dönemi için toplam 156 bin MWh enerji satış anlaşması yaptı. Anlaşmanın KDV hariç tutarı 500 milyon TL olarak açıklandı. Tutarın piyasa fiyatlarına göre değişebileceği belirtildi. Meka Global (MEKAG) – Suriye’de distribütörlük anlaşması Meka Global’in yüzde 100 bağlı ortaklığı Meka İthalat İhracat Pazarlama ve Ticaret A.Ş., Suriye’de faaliyet gösteren bir şirketle ürün satışına yönelik distribütörlük sözleşmesi imzaladı. Girişim Elektrik (GESAN) – 2,5 milyon dolarlık sözleşme Girişim Elektrik, Kahramanmaraş’ta gerçekleştirilecek Depolamalı Güneş Enerjisi Santrali projesinin enerji iletim hattı yapım işi için yurt içindeki bir müşteriyle 2,5 milyon dolar bedelli sözleşme imzaladı. Alcatel Lucent Teletaş (ALCTL) – 5,9 milyon dolarlık iş emri Alcatel Lucent Teletaş, Türkiye’de yerleşik bir müşteriyle devam eden iş ilişkisi kapsamında 5 milyon 896 bin 30 dolar tutarında iş emri imzaladığını duyurdu. Europower Enerji (EUPWR) – 1,13 milyar TL’lik TEİAŞ sözleşmesi Europower Enerji’nin yüzde 49 oranında ortak olduğu Euroes Teknoloji ve Taahhüt A.Ş., TEİAŞ’ın Konya Kuzey–IGA GES enerji iletim hattı yapım ihalesinde en avantajlı teklifi vermişti. Şirkete iletilen sözleşme davetinin ardından taraflar sözleşmeyi imzaladı. Sözleşmenin baz bedeli 1 milyar 133 milyon 133 bin 133 TL oldu. Anadolu Sigorta (ANSGR) – Brüt prim üretimi yüzde 18,5 arttı Anadolu Sigorta’nın 1 Ocak–31 Ekim 2026 dönemindeki bağımsız denetimden geçmemiş brüt prim üretimi 88 milyar 568 milyon 746 bin 439 TL’ye ulaştı. Böylece brüt prim üretimi geçen yılın aynı dönemine göre yüzde 18,5 artış gösterdi. Hun Yenilenebilir Enerji (HUNER) – Letonya’ya 6 milyon euroluk enerji depolama yatırımı Hun Yenilenebilir Enerji’nin yüzde 60 payını devraldığı Letonya merkezli SW Electricity SIA’nın Riga’da geliştirdiği yaklaşık 15 MW/30 MWh kapasiteli bataryalı enerji depolama projesinin inşaatına 2027 yılında başlanması planlanıyor. Projenin toplam yatırım tutarının yaklaşık 6 milyon euro olması bekleniyor. Finansman için Letonya’daki bankalardan teklifler alınırken kredi koşullarına ilişkin görüşmeler sürüyor. Gelecek Varlık Yönetimi (GLCVY) – 445,7 milyon TL’lik portföy ihalesi Gelecek Varlık Yönetimi, Fibabanka’nın 5 Kasım’da gerçekleştirdiği tahsili gecikmiş alacak satışında, 445,7 milyon TL anapara büyüklüğündeki bireysel portföyün ihalesini kazandı. İhale sonucunun kesinleşmesi için Fibabanka Yönetim Kurulu’nun onayı gerekiyor. Skyalp Finansal Teknolojiler (SKYLP) – 70,4 milyon TL’lik pay devri Skyalp Finansal Teknolojiler, iştiraki Tenk Bilişim Teknolojileri Danışmanlık A.Ş.’de sahip olduğu ve şirket sermayesinin yüzde 3,81’ine karşılık gelen 1 milyon 253 bin 122 adet payı, Hedef Portföy Gelişim Girişim Sermayesi Yatırım Fonu’na devretme kararı aldı. Pay devri için 70 milyon 387 bin TL bedel üzerinden sözleşme imzalandı. Gelirin Borsa Para Piyasası borçlarının ödenmesi ve işletme sermayesinde kullanılması planlanıyor. Deniz Gayrimenkul Yatırım Ortaklığı (DZGYO) – Bodrum’daki otel 979,4 milyon TL’ye satıldı Deniz Gayrimenkul Yatırım Ortaklığı, Bodrum’un Eskiçeşme Mahallesi’nde bulunan otel binasını KDV hariç 979 milyon 364 bin TL bedelle sattı. Gayrimenkulün ekspertiz değeri 968 milyon 700 bin TL olarak açıklanmıştı. Satış bedelinin 13 Kasım 2026 tarihinde tahsil edilmesi bekleniyor.

items.summaryTr: Paraguay’da yaklaşık 3 milyon müşterinin banka hesaplarına erişimini kaybetmesine yol açan Ueno krizinin ardından siyasi baskılar arttı. Devlet Başkanı Santiago Pena istifa ederken, Meclis’in azil sürecini onayladığı bildirildi.
items.articleText: Paraguay’da bankacılık krizi hükümeti devirdi: Devlet Başkanı Pena istifa etti - Paraguay’da yaklaşık 3 milyon müşterinin banka hesaplarına erişimini kaybetmesine yol açan Ueno krizinin ardından siyasi baskılar arttı. Devlet Başkanı Santiago Pena istifa ederken, Meclis’in azil sürecini onayladığı bildirildi. Paraguay’da dijital banka Ueno’nun çöküşüyle başlayan bankacılık krizi, ülkenin siyasi yönetimini de sarstı. Devlet Başkanı Santiago Pena, bankanın faaliyetlerinin durması ve milyonlarca müşterinin hesaplarına erişememesi üzerine artan siyasi baskılar nedeniyle Perşembe günü görevinden istifa etti. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Pena, yayımladığı video mesajında ülkenin istikrarını, toplumsal barışı ve demokratik kurumları koruma gerekliliğini göz önünde bulundurarak istifa kararı aldığını açıkladı. Bloomberg’in haberine göre Paraguay Meclisi, Pena’nın azledilmesini onayladı. İstifanın resmiyet kazanması için Senato’nun da kararı kabul etmesi gerekiyor. Ueno krizi 3 milyon müşteriyi etkiledi Yaklaşık 6,5 milyon nüfuslu Paraguay’da Ueno’nun faaliyetlerinin durdurulması, yaklaşık 3 milyon müşterinin banka hesaplarına erişememesine yol açtı. Ülke nüfusunun neredeyse yarısını etkileyen kriz, hükümet üzerindeki baskıyı artırdı. Paraguay Merkez Bankası, Ueno’nun asgari sermaye yeterliliği koşullarını ihlal ettiğini tespit etmesinin ardından bankaya el koydu. Başlangıçta sınırlı ölçekte faaliyet gösteren bir finansal teknoloji şirketi olan Ueno, hızlı büyümesinin ardından yaklaşık 850 milyon dolarlık kamu fonunu yöneten orta ölçekli bir bankaya dönüşmüştü. Kriz kapsamında Paraguay Merkez Bankası Başkanı da Salı günü istifa etti. Bankanın sekiz yöneticisi ise gözaltına alındı. items.title: French protests see numbers surge as unions join strikes over high cost of living
items.summary: The interior ministry estimates 600,000 people joined protests across France, while the unions say the number was far higher.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: French protests see numbers surge as unions join strikes over high cost of living
items.summaryTr: The interior ministry estimates 600,000 people joined protests across France, while the unions say the number was far higher.
items.articleText: French protests see numbers surge as unions join strikes over high cost of living - Published More than 600,000 protesters have taken part in rallies and marches across France, according to France's interior ministry, with five unions joining a day of action demanding more money for wages and public services. The left-wing CGT union put the number of people taking part in Thursday's mobilisation at 1.57 million and hailed the figure as "a level unmatched" since 2023, citing big protests in Paris, Marseille, Bordeaux and Lille. As darkness fell in Paris, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said he would convene a "social conference" with unions and employers next Monday. The wave of protests began in September over poor conditions and resources at lycées (high schools), before spreading to universities, workers and a revived "yellow-vest" movement against high prices. The unions had vowed to take the co-ordinated move against the government "to the next level", and CGT chief Sophie Binet had said their message was that "the only thing that will bring this mobilisation to a halt is responding to our demands". Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez had earlier deployed 70,000 police, vowing "an extremely firm response" to any potential outbreaks of violence. Some unrest was reported in several cities. A car was set alight near the Gallieni bridge over the Rhône river in Lyon, as hundreds of activists from the radical left-wing "black bloc" clashed with police. Clashes were also reported in the north-western city of Rennes, where the local prefect said a "hostile group of masked individuals" had gathered in front of the main union march. Tear gas was used to clear a square in the south-western city of Bordeaux and a teenager was hurt in a stabbing involving a student at a high-school blockade in the Seine-Saint-Denis suburb of northern Paris. But the trouble was not on the scale seen during the last big day of protests, on Saturday 17 October, when more than 2,000 stores were looted and historic buildings set on fire. The provisional numbers reported on Thursday were higher than on 17 October, considered the biggest day of rallies until now when the interior ministry said 550,000 people had turned out and the unions counted 800,000. Earlier on Thursday the leader of the CFDT union, Marylise Léon, said she would be happy if the protests matched that earlier level. A coalition of unions across the public and private sector had urged workers, pensioners and young people to join Thursday's day of strikes to intensify pressure on the government. In particular they are seeking a rise in the minimum wage, or Smic, which is currently €12.31 (£10) an hour. Sophie Binet told reporters at the start of a march in central Paris that protesters had "just reached a new level in their mobilisation" and were demanding immediate answers. An estimated 9.89% of civil servants were taking part in the strikes, according to government figures. Disruption was reported in schools, hospitals and public transport, and the Eiffel Tower and some exhibition rooms at the Louvre museum in Paris had to close. Workers were also asked to halt production at oil refineries and France was expected to import more electricity than it produced on Thursday because of disruption at nuclear plants. The head of the CFDT complained that it was not just the minimum wage that needed to increase. "We are asking for a net increase of €100 a month," Marylise Léon explained. The government has sought to appease public anger over rising prices, bringing down the cost of fuel by releasing 10 million barrels of diesel from strategic reserves. Ministers have also promised school students to reform the unpopular Parcoursup university admissions platform and eventually replace it by 2028. The prime minister said early on Thursday evening that Monday's "social conference" with unions and employers would seek to "provide answers to questions surrounding purchasing power and wages". However, the government by its own admission has little room to manoeuvre, as it looks to make tens of billions of euros in savings, in a bid to cut the budget deficit to 5% of GDP. The education ministry said that 16% of teachers had gone on strike on Thursday, and the unions said disruption had affected more than one in four lycées, which cater for 15-18 year-olds, as well as the vast majority of universities. "Now it's not only about [investing in] public services in education and higher education, it's about all of the public services in France," the vice-president of the Unef student union, Alice De Brito, told the BBC. Meanwhile, a revived gilets jaunes (yellow-vest) movement that staged a revolt against the high cost of living several years ago has called for further blockades and protests on Friday and Saturday too. Thursday's march was eventually allowed in central Paris, although not along the route proposed by the unions between Place de la Bastille and Place de la Concorde, which would have taken protesters near the National Assembly, the Élysée Palace, and the prime minister's residence at Hôtel Matignon. Instead, the march followed another central route from Place de la République to Place de la Nation. The interior minister had earlier spoken of three potential risks on Thursday, from radical left "black blocs" groups and looting to wildcat marches without union authorisation. - Published4 days ago

items.title: Shares in Musk's SpaceX plunge as tech and AI stocks fall
items.summary: The market has been reacting to possible tougher scrutiny of data centre construction and the AI industry following the US mid-terms
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Shares in Musk's SpaceX plunge as tech and AI stocks fall
items.summaryTr: The market has been reacting to possible tougher scrutiny of data centre construction and the AI industry following the US mid-terms
items.articleText: Shares in Musk's SpaceX plunge as tech and AI stocks fall - Published Shares in Elon Musk's SpaceX have plunged as tech and artificial intelligence stocks more broadly plummeted a day after the Democrats swept to victory in the midterms. Those losses dragged the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite stock index down, which had fallen by more than 5% at one point in early trading. The market has been reacting to possible tougher scrutiny of data centre construction and the artificial intelligence (AI) industry following Democrat wins in key data centre states including Texas. Following the election, some tech leaders have acknowledged they need to improve their communication around data centres and the benefits of AI. SpaceX shares were down more than 9% in by lunchtime in Thursday trading, while Tesla shares dropped more than 11%. Musk had spent nearly $450m backing Republican campaigns, including at least $45m in support of Ken Paxton for the Texas senate seat, but Texas was turned blue in the Democratic tsunami on Tuesday night. Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa campaigned heavily against data centres, pledging a moratorium on new construction in the sector. Shares in chipmakers have been suffering, with AMD dropping more than 14% on Thursday, while Micron shares had dropped by as much as 17% before recovering slightly. Intel shares are down by more than 7% and shares in Nvidia have fallen nearly 9%, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index had fallen by 10%. The stock falls also hit the S&P 500 index, which dropped by 3.8% by lunchtime. Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, said the steep sell-off on the Nasdaq and the S&P 500 was sending shockwaves into other markets. "Fresh panic over the AI trade has hit Wall Street hard," she said. "Fears that the vast sums poured into AI infrastructure may not deliver the returns investors have been banking on are now colliding with the prospect of a sharp slowdown in data centre construction." Some tech leaders have said they were caught off guard by the backlash against data centres in the midterms. OpenAI president and co-founder Greg Brockman said he believed everyone had been surprised by the reaction to data centres, and more work needed to be done to ensure communities were on board. "A lot of our shift over the course of this year has really been to realise that from San Francisco trying to build infrastructure in Texas, Georgia, and other places, you can't just tweet and say: 'This is going to be good.' You need to be in those communities," Brockman said at the WSJ Tech conference in Napa, California on Wednesday evening. Meta's president Dina Powell McCormick agreed that the industry needed to improve their communication about the benefits of AI. "I think we need to double and triple down on telling the story," she told the WSJ conference. Alongside the immediate impacts of the US mid-term elections, some investors have become concerned that AI shares could be in a bubble that is due a correction.

items.articleText: Tofaş'tan (TOASO) beklentileri aşan 3.çeyrek bilançosu: İşte detaylar! - Tofaş, 2026’nın ilk 9 ayında 10,97 milyar TL net kâr açıkladı. Şirketin üçüncü çeyrek kârı 4,33 milyar TL ile analistlerin 2,51 milyar TL’lik medyan beklentisini geride bıraktı. Tofaş Türk Otomobil Fabrikası A.Ş. (TOASO), 2026 yılı üçüncü çeyrek finansal sonuçlarını 5 Kasım 2026 tarihinde Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu’nda (KAP) açıkladı. Şirketin hem çeyreklik hem de dokuz aylık kârında güçlü artış kaydedildi. Tofaş’ın net kârı 9 ayda yüzde 189 arttı CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Tofaş, 1 Ocak–30 Eylül 2026 döneminde toplam 10 milyar 972 milyon 737 bin TL net kâr elde etti. Şirket, 2025’in aynı döneminde 3 milyar 802 milyon 128 bin TL kâr açıklamıştı. Böylece net kâr yıllık bazda yüzde 189 arttı. Şirketin 2026 yılının üçüncü çeyreğindeki net kârı ise 4 milyar 331 milyon 820 bin TL oldu. Satış gelirleri yüzde 21 yükseldi Tofaş’ın satış gelirleri, 2026’nın ilk dokuz ayında geçen yılın aynı dönemine göre yüzde 21 artarak 293 milyar 540 milyon 755 bin TL’ye ulaştı. 2025’in ilk dokuz ayında satışlar 245 milyar 788 milyon 653 bin TL seviyesindeydi. Esas faaliyet kârı da geçen yılın aynı dönemindeki 625 milyon 350 bin TL’lik zarardan 2026’nın ilk dokuz ayında 5 milyar 552 milyon 458 bin TL kâra döndü. Şirketin FAVÖK’ü ise 6 milyar 723 milyon 350 bin TL’den 7 milyar 533 milyon 739 bin TL’ye yükseldi. Tofaş’ın varlıkları ve özkaynakları 30 Eylül 2026 itibarıyla Tofaş’ın toplam varlıkları 212 milyar 199 milyon 178 bin TL oldu. Şirketin toplam borçları 139 milyar 418 milyon 250 bin TL, özkaynakları ise 72 milyar 780 milyon 928 bin TL olarak kaydedildi. Şirketin piyasa değeri 111,80 milyar TL seviyesinde bulunurken F/K oranı 6,37, PD/DD oranı 1,54 olarak açıklandı. Tofaş bilançosu beklentileri aştı Matriks Haber tarafından gerçekleştirilen bilanço anketine 12 aracı kurum katıldı. Ankete göre Tofaş’ın 2026 üçüncü çeyrek net kârı için ortalama beklenti 2 milyar 507 milyon 100 bin TL, medyan beklenti ise 2 milyar 513 milyon TL oldu. Şirketin açıkladığı 4 milyar 331 milyon 820 bin TL’lik net kâr, hem ortalama hem de medyan beklentinin belirgin şekilde üzerinde gerçekleşti. Böylece Tofaş, üçüncü çeyrek bilançosuyla analist beklentilerini aştı.

Satış gelirleri yüzde 21 yükseldi Tofaş’ın satış gelirleri, 2026’nın ilk dokuz ayında geçen yılın aynı dönemine göre yüzde 21 artarak 293 milyar 540 milyon 755 bin TL’ye ulaştı. 2025’in ilk dokuz ayında satışlar 245 milyar 788 milyon 653 bin TL seviyesindeydi. Şirketin piyasa değeri 111,80 milyar TL seviyesinde bulunurken F/K oranı 6,37, PD/DD oranı 1,54 olarak açıklandı. Tofaş bilançosu beklentileri aştı Matriks Haber tarafından gerçekleştirilen bilanço anketine 12 aracı kurum katıldı. Ankete göre Tofaş’ın 2026 üçüncü çeyrek net kârı için ortalama beklenti 2 milyar 507 milyon 100 bin TL, medyan beklenti ise 2 milyar 513 milyon TL oldu. Şirketin açıkladığı 4 milyar 331 milyon 820 bin TL’lik net kâr, hem ortalama hem de medyan beklentinin belirgin şekilde üzerinde gerçekleşti. items.summaryTr: The move follows a bank collapse and after the lower house of congress voted in favour of pursuing an impeachment trial against him.
items.articleText: Paraguay President Santiago Peña resigns after bank collapse - Published Paraguay's President Santiago Peña has announced his resignation following a political crisis sparked by the collapse of a bank linked to him. "I want to apologise to the people if at any point I failed," he said in a video message on social media. "It was never my intention to betray the trust you placed in me." The crisis erupted after Ueno Bank entered an insolvency process, which froze all operations. Lawmakers accused Peña, who was a shareholder until last year in the company that owned the bank, of conflicts of interest and misconduct. Peña has rejected suggestions of impropriety. His resignation comes after Paraguay's lower house of congress voted in favour of pursuing an impeachment trial. In his video message posted on X, Peña said his resignation was to protect stability, social peace and democratic institutions. Ueno Bank has said it has about three million customers, equivalent to about 60% of Paraguay's adult population. It held pensions and some other public funds and, after its collapse earlier this week, millions could not access their accounts. The central bank seized the digital lender, and people took to the streets protesting and demanding Peña's resignation. A new president of the Central Bank of Paraguay has been appointed and Congress has approved a process to pay depositors. Peña won election in 2023 representing Paraguay's ruling conservative Colorado Party, beating a centre-left challenger.

items.titleTr: Paraguay president resigns after collapse of Ueno digital bank
items.summaryTr: Santiago Peña stepped down amid mounting scrutiny over his former ties to Ueno Bank’s parent company, as the lender’s collapse left millions of customers unable to access their funds.
items.articleText: Paraguay president resigns after collapse of Ueno digital bank Santiago Peña stepped down amid mounting scrutiny over his former ties to Ueno Bank’s parent company, as the lender’s collapse left millions of customers unable to access their funds. Paraguayan President Santiago Peña announced his resignation Thursday amid a deepening political crisis triggered by the collapse of digital lender Ueno Bank. In a video posted to X, Peña said he was stepping down to preserve the country’s stability, social peace and democratic institutions. He added that his priority was protecting Paraguayans who had entrusted their savings to the financial system. Paraguay’s central bank announced resolution proceedings for Ueno Bank on Tuesday after finding that its solvency ratio had fallen below half of the regulatory minimum. Peña faced mounting political scrutiny over his former business ties to Grupo Vázquez, the conglomerate that controls Ueno Bank. He remained a business partner of the group until March 2025, according to AP. Peña has denied any wrongdoing, arguing that the controversy began as a regulatory matter before escalating into a political dispute. The banking crisis also coincided with elevated asking prices for Tether’s USDt on Bybit’s Paraguay-facing peer-to-peer marketplace. One listing viewed early Thursday offered USDt at 6,942 Paraguayan guaraníes, approximately 13% above the central bank’s Nov. 4 reference rate of 6,144.02 guaraníes per US dollar. His resignation came as lawmakers debated impeachment proceedings over alleged conflicts of interest, misuse of pension funds and institutional cover-ups linked to Ueno Bank’s collapse, according to Reuters. Peña, who was elected in April 2023 and took office that August, was serving a five-year term scheduled to end in 2028. Under Paraguay’s Constitution, Vice President Pedro Alliana would succeed him for the remainder of the term if Congress accepts his resignation. Ueno Bank’s collapse affects millions of customers Ueno Bank had grown rapidly since 2021 into one of Paraguay’s largest financial institutions, serving more than 3 million customers in a country of roughly 6.5 million people. Ueno first came under regulatory scrutiny in June over loans to companies linked to its controlling shareholder, Grupo Vázquez. In an October statement, the bank acknowledged receiving regulatory notices on June 5 and July 24 requiring adjustments to its related-party lending exposure. On Nov. 2, the Central Bank of Paraguay initiated resolution proceedings after adjustments to the bank’s financial statements pushed its solvency ratio below half the regulatory minimum. Authorities suspended the bank’s operations, restricting customers’ access to their deposits. Paraguayan authorities detained eight Ueno Bank executives on Nov. 3, including Grupo Vázquez president Miguel Vázquez and bank president Juan Manuel Gustale, according to local newspaper ABC Color. A court subsequently ordered six executives held in pretrial detention and placed two others under house arrest. Paraguay begins depositor payouts amid protests On Thursday, Paraguay’s central bank announced that it would start deposit guarantee payments to eligible clients with balances of up to 10 million guaraníes (about $1,630), provided they had no outstanding debts to Ueno and held accounts at other financial institutions. Under the country’s deposit insurance system, deposits are protected up to 228.3 million guaraníes (about $37,200) per depositor, per financial institution. The bank’s collapse sparked protests in the nation’s capital, Asunción, where hundreds of depositors, pensioners and workers demanded the return of their savings and accountability from government officials. This is a developing story. We will update this article as more information becomes available.

items.title: Hoax bomb threats target European airlines and airports for second time in a week
items.summary: At least 21 flights across Europe are affected in what the UK government calls a "malicious hoax threat".
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Hoax bomb threats target European airlines and airports for second time in a week
items.summaryTr: At least 21 flights across Europe are affected in what the UK government calls a "malicious hoax threat".
items.articleText: Hoax bomb threats target European airlines and airports for second time in a week - Published At least 21 aircraft and several airports across Europe have been targeted by bomb threats in the second such incident this week, with the UK calling it a "malicious hoax". Flights to Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, France, Italy, Poland and Romania were affected. An Aer Lingus plane from Dublin to Rome was diverted to an air base in France and Italian fighter jets escorted Finnair's Helsinki-Rome flight. EasyJet said its flights from Newcastle and Glasgow were met by police in Prague as a precaution. London Heathrow and Birmingham airports received threats that were assessed as not credible. No explosives have been found during searches, and it is not clear if the incidents, some claimed by a little known group, are related. - Who could be behind hoax bomb threats to European air travel? - Published50 minutes ago The airport authorities in Italy's capital Rome said the hoax threat against two inbound flights received on Thursday had come by email. The warnings were signed on behalf of a group or individual calling themselves "Fighters of the Male State", claiming to be targeting a "feminist regime" and wanting to "make our mark on history". They threatened to "turn the skies red" with explosions. These details were first reported by Italian media and then confirmed to the BBC by Aeroporti di Roma, which manages both of the city airports. "Fighters of the Male State" likely refers to the Russian group "Muzhskoi Legion" ( "Male Legion") - an ultra-right group with such extreme views it was banned by a Moscow court in 2021. Yet it retained tens of thousands of online followers as it cheered on the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine in the following year. But that email, even if genuine, is unlikely to provide the leads that police and airport authorities need to pin down who is generating these hoaxes and why. UK Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander described Thursday's incidents as "malicious hoax threats." She said the government was taking "these threats seriously", stressing that there were "established processes for dealing with hoax and malicious threats". A UK government spokesperson later said the threats reported "in the early hours" of the day had been "resolved", without giving any further details. Heathrow later said in a statement it had received a threat earlier in the day which was "deemed not credible", adding there was "no risk to passengers, colleagues or the aircraft". "There are robust UK aviation security standards in place to assess and safely manage these types of situations," the statement said. Meanwhile, a Birmingham Airport spokesperson told the BBC it had received a threat, after which "processes were immediately initiated in conjunction with emergency services and partners". The following flights were targeted by threats on Thursday: - Aer Lingus said its flight from Dublin to Rome diverted to Normandy, landing safely. The company added that it was working to "re-accommodate customers to their final destination as soon as possible". - Two Finnair flights from Helsinki landed at their destinations as normal, the airline said. One was escorted into Rome's Fiumicino airport by Italian Air Force fighter jets, Aeroporti di Roma told the BBC, while the other landed in Vienna, Austria - Wizz Air said two flights which departed Milan were affected - one was heading to Warsaw, before being diverting to Vienna; the other landed safely in Bucharest, with teams inspecting the aircraft - Polish airline LOT said its flight from Warsaw to Brussels landed as planned, and "no suspicious items were found". Another LOT flight from Warsaw to Paris was stopped before take-off and the plane and baggage underwent a security screening, with no hazardous items found - Three Ryanair flights landed in Bulgaria, according to Bulgarian media - one from Copenhagen and another from Madrid landed in the capital Sofia, while a third coming from London bound for Sofia landed in Plovdiv. The flights were escorted by Bulgarian air force fighter jets - No explosives were found on four flights which landed in Prague, Czech police said. EasyJet later said its flights from Newcastle and Glasgow were among those affected. "Passengers on both flights disembarked normally," the company said - Aegean Airlines said it "was informed of a bomb threat" concerning two of its flights from Thessaloniki in Greece to Milan, and also from Athens to Vienna. It said threat was "unfounded", and both flights departed from the respective airports" - A Ryanair flight from Porto in Portugal landed safely in Milan as planned, with bomb disposal experts checking them on arrival, Italy's Ansa news agency reported - Spain's airport authority said it had received bomb threats affecting three flights at Madrid airport, but any threat was ruled out following inspections. Iberia later said two of its flights - Milan-Madrid and Rome-Madrid - were affected. It was not clear whether the third plane was the above reported Ryanair Madrid to Sofia flight - Air Serbia said its flight from Belgrade to Bucharest "landed safely at its destination airport", and after checks, a reported bomb threat was "assessed as unfounded" Emily Noble, who was aboard the diverted Aer Lingus plane from Dublin to Rome, said she was about an hour into her flight to attend a friend's wedding in the Italian capital when passengers were told about a "technical" problem. Later, as the Aer Lingus plane began circling for an unplanned landing in France, the pilot said there was a "security" issue, the 26-year-old from Dublin told BBC Verify. On board it was "an odd experience," Noble said. "It was worrying because we didn't know what was going on, but we were all trying to be as calm as we could." Noble says she could hear fighter jets during the landing and saw one touch down behind the aircraft. After landing at the Évreux-Fauville air base in Normandy, passengers learned the flight had been the subject of a bomb threat. Noble said they remained on board for two-and-a-half hours while police and military personnel carried out checks, including searches with sniffer dogs. The passengers were later told they would be taken to an airport in Paris and another plane would fly them on to Rome. Philip Baum, professor of aviation security at the University of Coventry, said the industry "faces multiple bomb threats every single day" but he had been "surprised" by this week's incidents. A flight is diverted "only when the threat is credible and the authorities believe there is a potential of explosive device on board", he said. He said the concern was that "if you issue enough hoax threats, then complacency could set in and a real threat could be ignored - or they could be a diversion". Marco Chan, an aviation expert at Kingston University, told the BBC the threats were "most likely a hoax, but the system is right to treat it as real". He said they were being viewed by some experts as "possibly part of a pattern of cheap, deniable disruption" to air travel. Hoaxes can also come from copycats, he said, but "three days of incidents is too small a sample to separate coordination from contagion". Two days ago, seven European flights, including two from the UK, were searched after bomb threats were made. No explosives were found on any of the planes after searches. On Monday, a Wizz Air flight travelling from London Luton Airport to Sofia was escorted by a Hungarian fighter jet to Budapest after a mid-air bomb threat. Aracı kurumların radarındaki hisseler belli oldu YAYIN TARİHİ, 05 Kasım 2026 20:20 GÜNCELLEME, 05 Kasım 2026 20:33 PAYLAŞ 2026'nın üçüncü çeyrek bilanço dönemi devam ederken aracı kurumlar ve yatırım kuruluşları portföylerini ve borsada işlem gören şirket hisseleri için hedef fiyatlarını da hazırladı. İşte toplamda 8 hisse için yapılan hedef fiyat tahminleri... Borsa İstanbul’da işlem gören ve bilançosunu açıklayan 8 şirket için aracı kurumlardan yeni hedef fiyat ve yatırım tavsiyeleri geldi. Çimsa, Türk Traktör, Arçelik ve TAB Gıda’nın da aralarında bulunduğu hisselere yönelik değerlendirmelerde hedef fiyatlar ve tavsiyeler kurumlara göre farklılık gösterdi. İşte 8 hisse için açıklanan hedef fiyatlar ve aracı kurumların tavsiyeleri... TAB Gıda (TABGD) Lila Kağıt Sanayi ve Ticaret A.Ş. (LILAK) Türk Traktör (TTRAK) Agesa Hayat ve Emeklilik A.Ş. items.summary: Most analysts expected the increase from 3.75% to 4%.

items.titleTr: Interest rates hiked to 4% in first increase in over three years
items.summaryTr: Most analysts expected the increase from 3.75% to 4%.
items.articleText: Interest rates hiked to 4% in first increase in over three years - Published Interest rates have risen for the first time in more than three years and the Bank of England has signalled a further increase is likely unless the US-Iran war is resolved. Rates rose to 4% from 3.75% in a bid to curb inflation mainly driven by the conflict's impact on global oil prices. Andrew Bailey, the Bank's governor, said the decision "shouldn't be seen as the first in an inevitable long sequence of hikes", but warned "unless the conflict in the Middle East is resolved, neither does it seem likely to be the last increase". The higher level will increase the cost of borrowing for things such as mortgages, loans and credit cards, but will also lead to higher returns on savings. The Bank's rate-setting committee all backed increasing interest rates, with eight out of nine voting in favour of the rise to 4%. One member wanted an even bigger increase to 4.25%. Bailey said the hike was warranted due to higher energy prices and pointed to what happens in the Middle East as the main factor in future decisions. "Put simply, it requires real progress towards settling the conflict in the Middle East," the governor said. Bailey said he could "see the argument" for a further rate hike, before taking a "more conditional approach" dependent on the path of energy prices and inflation in the coming months. However, the views of members on the rate-setting committee differed on the path forward. Clare Lombardelli agreed there was "likely to be a case for a further increase in rates in the near term", while Megan Greene went further, suggesting "additional hikes" might be likely depending on how inflation impacted wages, prices and the jobs market. However, Alan Taylor said the rate rise was a "a risk-management 'one-for-now' insurance hike". Inflation, which measures the pace of price rises over time, is well below its peak of a few years ago but remains above the Bank of England's 2% target and is expected to increase further next year. Prices rose 3.5% in the year to September 2026, largely due to higher fuel prices. Millions of households are also set to be hit by energy bill increases in January. Higher fuel prices can lead to prices rising for a host of goods and staples as businesses pass on higher costs to customers. But the Bank said there was "limited evidence" this had happened so far for goods, such as food, with some firms absorbing cost increases and accepting lower margins. In an interview with the BBC, Bailey defended the decision to raise rates despite the Bank's assessment that inflation was yet to spread to other parts of the economy. He said further increases in energy prices are putting upward pressure on inflation and "that's what we have to seek to lean against". Patrick Bryson, from Brighton, is set to see his five-year mortgage term with a 3.51% interest rate end soon. The best deal the 51-year-old can find is a 5.17% loan with HSBC, which means his repayments will jump from £1,420 to £1,680 a month from February. "The only thing that bugs me about the mortgage is that after five years of paying it off we are now paying more than we were before," said the father-of-three. "That's a bit of a slap in the face." The guitar teacher, who has a combined income of around £68,000 a year with his wife, who manages a care home, said the couple is feeling pressure on their finances and so have changed their shopping habits and are looking to reduce their subcription outgoings. "Over the last year I have stopped buying wine, we don't go out to eat much anymore, we have knocked takeaways on the head. The prices are ridiculous," he said. - Three ways the interest rate rise could affect you - Published7 hours ago - Faisal Islam: How high will interest rates go? - Published7 hours ago The Bank now expects inflation to peak at 4.9% in the middle of next year, higher than it originally estimated, and not return to 2% until 2028. But in an "adverse scenario", where the US-Iran war could escalate further and send oil prices higher, inflation could reach 6.2% in 2027, it suggested. While the UK cannot control global energy prices, the Bank raised rates, for the first time since August 2023, in order to limit the knock-on effects of high energy prices resulting in inflation going up across the board. Its base rate is what it charges other banks and building societies to borrow money, which influences what customers for mortgages, loans, credit cards get charged, as well as savings rates. The rate rise will see 510,000 tracker mortgage-holders see a £31 monthly jump in repayments, according to banking trade body UK Finance. Homeowners on fixed deals will see no change, though future products may be affected. However, people on variable deals will be impacted depending on how their lender reacts to the rate rise. Typically a 0.25pp rise means a £14 increase per month in repayments. Get in touch Do you have a mortgage, a credit card, a car finance agreement? How are interest rates affecting you? - Published7 days ago

items.title: Russell Brand is being investigated over two new rape complaints, police say
items.summary: Det Supt Andy Furphy said he hoped other potential victims would gain "courage" and "confidence" from the guilty verdicts.

items.titleTr: Russell Brand is being investigated over two new rape complaints, police say
items.summaryTr: Det Supt Andy Furphy said he hoped other potential victims would gain "courage" and "confidence" from the guilty verdicts.
items.articleText: Russell Brand is being investigated over two new rape complaints, police say - Published Warning: Details of rape and sexual assault Russell Brand is being investigated over rape allegations made by two more women, it can now be reported. The disgraced comedian has been found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault by a jury of eight men and four women at Southwark Crown Court, following a three-week trial. More victims are likely to come forward following his conviction, the detective who led the police investigation has said. Det Supt Andy Furphy, from the Metropolitan Police, said he hoped other women would gain "courage" and "confidence" from the guilty verdicts. Brand was found not guilty of two counts of rape and one count of attempted indecent assault. 'Ruthless' Brand had initially been coy and quiet in police interviews, said Furphy, but became bolder as officers continued to question him. "As he gets used to something, he becomes more emboldened by it," Furphy said. "You can certainly see that in his offending." Hundreds of people were interviewed as part of the investigation and officers said several witnesses came forward, some of whom had previously had a sexual relationship with Brand. Katy Perry, the US singer who was married to Brand from 2010 to 2012, was not interviewed. Brand, 51, who was described in court as "ruthless" and a "sexual predator", was once one of the UK's most high-profile and in-demand entertainers. Some of the women said they had been left "haunted for years" by what he did to them. Speaking to the BBC, officers working on the three-year Metropolitan Police investigation described how bringing Brand to justice was not without its challenges. Allegations about Brand's behaviour first emerged in the media in September 2023. The Times, Sunday Times and Channel 4's Dispatches programme jointly reported that four women had accused him of rape, sexual assault and emotional abuse - claims he strongly denied. The investigation into other reports against Brand began soon after the story broke. "We kind of assumed that people might want to come forward," Furphy said, "and people came forward." Victim reports were made to forces across the country and the Met set up a dedicated team of officers to lead the investigation, which it called Operation Actinolite. Officers said they have since taken more than 340 witness statements - including from Brand's former employers, his ex-colleagues and associates. One officer was assigned to read Brand's books, watch his stand-up routines and DVDs and listen to his podcasts to help build the case. Brand's high profile and the intense media scrutiny around him proved a challenge to officers, said Furphy. Another complexity for the team was the allegations were all "non-recent". The earliest dated back 27 years. It meant there was no CCTV and no forensic evidence to work with. Furphy said police had to look for other ways to build their case. "Can we look at where the victims were at the time? Who did they speak to in the aftermath of it? Did they tell anybody else? What other available material is there for us to review that might lend some weight to it? Just because it's non-recent doesn't mean that we can't solve it at all." A former friend of Brand's was called to court to give evidence for the prosecution, while a statement from the parents of one of the women was heard. The entertainer's former personal assistant, who worked closely with Brand, told the jury about his "insane sexual appetite". 'Deeply uncomfortable' process Two months after the police investigation began, Brand was interviewed under caution for the first time. He was interviewed on two further occasions in the following months. In each interview he provided officers with a prepared statement, which said he did not recognise the complainants or recall the alleged incidents and that if any sexual activity had taken place, it would have been consensual. He then answered "no comment" to the officers' questions. Charges were brought against Brand in early April 2025: one count of rape, one count of oral rape, two charges of sexual assault and one allegation of indecent assault. The final charge would later be changed to attempted indecent assault at his trial. The charges all related to women who had come forward since the initial Channel 4 documentary. The following month he appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court, in London. He was swarmed by camera crews, so much so that it took him more than two minutes to walk the short distance to the court door. At a later court hearing he pleaded not guilty to the charges. Meanwhile, women continued to come forward with more allegations. In July 2025, Brand was interviewed for a fourth time before being charged with further offences: one count of rape and one count of sexual assault. He also denied those allegations. And then on 14 October 2026, accompanied by his wife Laura, the actor and comedian entered the glass dock at London's Southwark Crown Court for the start of his trial. The women each came to court and gave evidence to the jury from behind a screen, with Brand listening from the dock. At times they cried as they gave their evidence. Furphy believes there may be more women who will now come forward. "I think it's likely - potentially - that other women will come forward," he said. "They'll probably gain some courage and some confidence from what's happened in the courtroom over the last few weeks." He credits the women for their bravery during what has been at times a "deeply uncomfortable" process. "They are courageous, determined women and our focus has always been on them, not Russell Brand." Russell Brand on Trial You can follow analysis and further insights on the BBC podcast Russell Brand on Trial - available on BBC Sounds, YouTube, iPlayer, or wherever you get your BBC podcasts Related topics - Published6 days ago

items.title: Drunk and dangerous e-bike riders face on-the-spot fines under crackdown
items.summary: A consultation will consider fines and other ways to clamp down on dangerous e-bike riders.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Drunk and dangerous e-bike riders face on-the-spot fines under crackdown
items.summaryTr: A consultation will consider fines and other ways to clamp down on dangerous e-bike riders.
items.articleText: Drunk and dangerous e-bike riders face on-the-spot fines under crackdown - Published People riding drunk or dangerously on e-bikes – and those who jump red lights - could face on-the-spot fines under plans to curb anti-social behaviour. Firms which run shared e-bike schemes will also be expected to manage their fleets better and provide designated parking areas to keep pavements safe. They could also be required to take out insurance so people can claim compensation if they are hit by someone on a shared bike. It's part of a crackdown on what ministers called the "wild west" of e-biking – with a patchwork of rules across the country often leaving the streets unsafe for pedestrians. A consultation launched on Thursday sets out proposed national standards to make journeys safer for everyone and keep pavements clear, particularly for wheelchair users and families with prams. The first e-bikes were launched in Exeter in 2016 and arrived in London a year later, growing to become a popular commuter option. According to the Greater London Authority, 37 million trips were taken on dockless e-bikes last year – a third more than the previous year. Shared e-bikes - such as Lime, Voi, Beryl, Dott, Forest and Bolt - make short journeys quick and convenient. While some areas enforce rules that mean shared bikes can only be left in specific areas, others have looser rules. Under the government's proposals, local leaders will be able to license schemes in their area, allowing them to enforce minimum standards and better integrate e-bikes into existing transport networks. Measures could include requiring operators to have a parking plan and to manage fleet sizes and operating areas, so bikes aren't overcrowding streets. The consultation will also consider ways to tackle antisocial and illegal behaviour, to prevent users from riding shared cycles drunk, underage, or on pavements. There will also be clear consequences set out – such as fines - for this type of behaviour. The government is also consulting on whether local leaders should have extra powers, including setting fees and requirements for operators to share data to improve enforcement and journey planning. The consultation will last for eight weeks after which the government will draw up legislation to implement the changes. - 'Dumped e-scooters force blind people into road' - Published1 April - Red light jumping cyclists offered film over fine - Published14 October - 'Our lives will never be the same again after Lime bike crash' - Published29 June Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the e-bike clampdown was a "small but important everyday fix" which would make streets safer. Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander said the government wanted e-bike schemes to "grow in popularity" but acknowledged they were "causing a little bit of nuisance at the moment". Asked how punishments for dangerous cycling could be enforced, Alexander said licensing rules could allow for fines but added: "What you can't do is legislate for every eventuality, you can't legislate for idiots." "The police enforce the rules of the road to stop cyclists when they are behaving recklessly but police have got a lot on their plate so individuals have to take some responsibility," she added. Bosses at Lime, Voi and Bolt all welcomed the proposals, adding that consistent standards being applied across the country would provide clarity and certainty for operators, riders and the general public. Mike Wordingham from the Royal National Institute for the Blind said 92% of blind and partially sighted people had been forced to walk into roads due to e-bikes blocking pavements. He welcomed the government's announced but warned that tackling rider behaviour would be "difficult" and said a locally-led approach shouldn't lead to "a patchwork of regulations and inconsistency in implementing them". It's part of a crackdown on what ministers called the "wild west" of e-biking – with a patchwork of rules across the country often leaving the streets unsafe for pedestrians. A consultation launched on Thursday sets out proposed national standards to make journeys safer for everyone and keep pavements clear, particularly for wheelchair users and families with prams. The first e-bikes were launched in Exeter in 2016 and arrived in London a year later, growing to become a popular commuter option. According to the Greater London Authority, 37 million trips were taken on dockless e-bikes last year – a third more than the previous year. Shared e-bikes - such as Lime, Voi, Beryl, Dott, Forest and Bolt - make short journeys quick and convenient. While some areas enforce rules that mean shared bikes can only be left in specific areas, others have looser rules. Under the government's proposals, local leaders will be able to license schemes in their area, allowing them to enforce minimum standards and better integrate e-bikes into existing transport networks. Measures could include requiring operators to have a parking plan and to manage fleet sizes and operating areas, so bikes aren't overcrowding streets. The consultation will also consider ways to tackle antisocial and illegal behaviour, to prevent users from riding shared cycles drunk, underage, or on pavements. There will also be clear consequences set out – such as fines - for this type of behaviour. The government is also consulting on whether local leaders should have extra powers, including setting fees and requirements for operators to share data to improve enforcement and journey planning. The consultation will last for eight weeks after which the government will draw up legislation to implement the changes. - 'Dumped e-scooters force blind people into road' - Published1 April - Red light jumping cyclists offered film over fine - Published14 October - 'Our lives will never be the same again after Lime bike crash' - Published29 June Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the e-bike clampdown was a "small but important everyday fix" which would make streets safer. Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander said the government wanted e-bike schemes to "grow in popularity" but acknowledged they were "causing a little bit of nuisance at the moment". Asked how punishments for dangerous cycling could be enforced, Alexander said licensing rules could allow for fines but added: "What you can't do is legislate for every eventuality, you can't legislate for idiots." "The police enforce the rules of the road to stop cyclists when they are behaving recklessly but police have got a lot on their plate so individuals have to take some responsibility," she added. Bosses at Lime, Voi and Bolt all welcomed the proposals, adding that consistent standards being applied across the country would provide clarity and certainty for operators, riders and the general public. Mike Wordingham from the Royal National Institute for the Blind said 92% of blind and partially sighted people had been forced to walk into roads due to e-bikes blocking pavements. He welcomed the government's announced but warned that tackling rider behaviour would be "difficult" and said a locally-led approach shouldn't lead to "a patchwork of regulations and inconsistency in implementing them". items.titleTr: Why do veterinary fees and sausage rolls vary in price across London?
items.summaryTr: Location is not just the only factor on why prices differ across London, as Anna O'Neill finds out.
items.articleText: Why do veterinary fees and sausage rolls vary in price across London? - Published Have you ever wondered why the same item costs more or less depending on where in London you buy it? Take a bog standard Greggs’ sausage roll for example. If you buy it in an outer London borough like Sutton, it costs £1.35. But if you buy it in central London you're likely to pay £1.60. You might have guessed that the price difference, according to Greggs, is often about location. "We use national pricing across most of our shops however, this can vary in certain locations where costs are higher than average, such as travel hubs," they told the BBC in a statement. So far so obvious perhaps. What about going out for pizza? You might think the price of a pizza at the same chain would be the same wherever in London you eat it. Not necessarily. A Duo Romana pizza from Pizza Express costs £20.95 in Muswell Hill, north London. But three miles (5km) further north in Southgate, the same pizza at Pizza Express costs a pound more. And in central London the same pizza will set you back £22.95. Pizza Express was asked for comment but did not respond. Consumer expert Helen Dewdney from the Complaining Cow, external website says that as well as higher costs in central London, the price difference can also be due to how convenient it is to get to the restaurant. Southgate has a Tube station, Muswell Hill does not. "It’s all about cashing in on convenience for people. "One will be nearer a Tube, so they’re counting on people saying 'Oh, I'll just get a pizza on the way home'. "Whereas another you might have to make a journey to it." Other examples of cross-borough price variations include: - A Vue cinema ticket bought online costs £6.99 in Eltham, but £9.99 in Piccadilly or Angel, Islington - A blow dry at Rush hair salon costs from £45 in Kentish Town, north London but £40 in Ilford, east London - Fish, chips and a drink in Wetherspoons in Sidcup, south-east London costs £11.18 but the same meal in Camden Town, north London costs £12.77. Also, petrol prices can vary from pump to pump at the same company and within as little as a mile (1.5km) radius. A recent example from EG On the Move on the same day in London found these price variations: - Unleaded (E10): 171.9p – 177.9p per litre - Diesel (B7): 198.2p – 201.9p. Other forecourts also charge more or less if they are near a main road or a motorway or part of a supermarket for example. For this Dewdney recommends downloading a price comparison app like petrolprices.com, external "You can look at the distance as well as the price difference so you’re not driving too far away," she explained. "It’s not always the nearest one that’s worth going to." Vet bills are another example. Recent changes to legislation mean that vets must publish a comprehensive price list for standard services but it does not necessarily follow that vets in a different practice at the same chain will have the same prices. Vets for Pets in Pets At Home is a case in point. In Pets At Home in Chingford, east London the Vets for Pets practice charges £136 for a rabbit castration including two follow-up consultations. The same treatment at Vets For Pets in Pets At Home in Enfield, north London costs £70. Dewdney admits being surprised that the price can almost double from one practice to another. "I think it's an interesting one, because... they can set their own prices. "Although the government did bring in some changes for vets, it wasn't about capping the prices. It was just that they had to be more transparent," she explained. Pets At Home said: "Vets for Pets practices are independently owned and operated, with practice owners having full clinical and day-to-day operational autonomy, including setting fees for delivering the high-quality care and services they provide. "Pricing decisions are made locally and vary for many reasons including factors such as operating costs, staffing, facilities and the unique needs of the communities they serve. "All costs are communicated clearly with clients ahead of any treatment or service being provided." The company also said that veterinary practices had, like many businesses across the UK "experienced increased operating costs over the past year, including rises in energy, wages, medicines and other essential supplies". It added: "These pressures are felt right across the sector, but practice teams work hard to keep costs as low as possible to ensure high-quality care is accessible and affordable for pet owners in their local communities." So what is the moral of the story? Perhaps to shop around, and not to assume that prices at the same chain will be the same wherever you go, whether that be for veterinary care, your weekly shop, having your hair done or filling up the car. Price comparison websites can be a useful tool, and it is worth remembering that just because goods may be from the same restaurant, supermarket or petrol station in a different area, prices may well vary. Or as Dewdney summed up: "People have just got to do their research." items.title: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
items.articleText: Release Number 9321-26 CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets November 04, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the U.S. Department of Agriculture today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to safeguard the integrity of U.S. agricultural markets. The MOU will allow the CFTC and USDA to harmonize policies and practices to better share information and increase access to risk management tools. The agreement will also assist both agencies with monitoring and identifying structural or potential systematic risks, among other things. “For decades, America’s agricultural community has relied on our markets to hedge risk, manage uncertainty, and plan for the future,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I’m proud that the CFTC and USDA have formalized this partnership through an MOU that will strengthen protections for America’s farmers, ranchers, and producers while expanding opportunities to manage risk through more efficient data sharing. I commend Secretary Rollins for her partnership and commitment to a more coordinated regulatory approach that safeguards the integrity of our markets and ensures they continue serving the agricultural community that feeds and clothes our nation.” “Faster and more transparent data sharing between USDA and CFTC is critical to helping our farmers and ranchers navigate an ever-changing market,” said USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins. “This MOU builds upon USDA’s ongoing data modernization efforts and allows our agencies to collaboratively identify risks and improve responses to market events. Breaking down barriers between government agencies to deliver for our customers is a hallmark of this administration and I am looking forward to the successes this MOU will bring.” -CFTC-

items.title: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
items.articleText: Release Number 9320-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas entered a default judgment against defendants Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for their participation in a commodities fraud scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented they would use participant funds to trade futures and options, including those involving natural gas, oil, and gold; made material misrepresentations and omissions about the profitability of commodity trading with them; and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying Larrick’s personal expenses, and sending funds to offshore accounts in Costa Rica. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,767,625 civil monetary penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution. It also permanently enjoined them from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposed permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2023 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8768-23.] -CFTC-

items.title: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
items.articleText: Release Number 9319-26 CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig today released a statement announcing that perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities can begin trading for the first time on designated contract markets that are dually registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as notice-registered national securities exchanges to trade security futures products. Key excerpts from Chairman Selig’s statement: “Today, perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities (the ‘Equity Perps’) can begin trading for the first time on CFTC-registered exchanges. … “This expansion marks a significant step towards allowing U.S. market participants, consistent with applicable law, to avail themselves of the advantages of perpetual futures that have led to their emergence as widely sought tools for risk-management and price-discovery. I believe that bringing these types of innovative products into our regulated markets ensures that American investors and traders can access these products within the protections of the CFTC’s proven regulatory framework, rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues. … “The Equity Perps build on the foundation of the [Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000] and the [CFTC-SEC Memorandum of Understanding]. For too long, regulatory uncertainty left innovative products, such as security futures and equity perpetual futures, stranded in what SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins has aptly described as a regulatory ‘no man’s land’ due to a lack of harmonization between the agencies. The CFTC and SEC have turned the page on that era, and are committed to delivering regulatory clarity for innovative products and a clear path to market, rather than more casualties of jurisdictional disputes.” Read Chairman Selig’s full statement here. -CFTC-

items.title: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
items.articleText: Release Number 9318-26 CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced it will host an industry roundtable Dec. 15 to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The dialogue will build upon the CFTC’s Request for Comment earlier this summer on 24/7 trading. The CFTC’s roundtable will provide a public venue for dialogue on the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. Participants will convene from across the industry to discuss how the Commission can promote responsible innovation while protecting market participants and preserving the integrity and resilience of U.S. derivatives markets. “I have been consistently clear: under my leadership, the CFTC will not take a one‑size‑fits‑all approach to 24/7 trading. Market structure evolves best through thoughtful and responsible progress, and that’s exactly why we’re hosting a roundtable to hear directly from industry on their views for 24/7 trading across different asset classes,” Chairman Selig said. The roundtable will take place at CFTC’s headquarters in Washington. Information regarding the agenda, speakers, and registration will be posted at a later date. This event will be open to the public and livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Please note the number of in-person participants may be limited, and visitors will be subject to security checks. Members of the public are welcome to submit speaker nominations to [email protected]. -CFTC-
